narrative: TR-B01-R090 was not following the rest of the block. Controller reset did not take so swapped the gearbox out. Came back after lunch to verify and it is tracking with the block now.

KVP36-1635C-0375 threw a DC ground fault alarm. Isolated the fault down to CB-B06-05 where I found a home run chafed through against the rack upright. Repaired the run and resecured it clear of the steel with a proper standoff. Insulation resistance verified normal on the affected string before restoration. Unit returned to service and the fault has not recurred since.
Row TR-Z05 was out of alignment with the rest of the block. Recalibrated the limits and it is tracking normal now.
Near miss reported. Loose grating at the B05 skid entry, someone nearly went through it. Secured it and tagged it for a proper repair. idk how long it had been like that.

Quarterly site walk on B02. Cable sag noted on the north rows, roughly eight spans hanging lower than they should. Checked the clips on those spans, most have failed at the fixing rather than the cable having pulled through. Rest of the block is in good order. Recommend the rework is scheduled before the next mow cycle rather than after.
kvp24-1906a-0149 fan fault, bird nest in the plenum, cleared
MV CABLE FAULT between B01 and the collector. Locator put it around 300 ft in. Contractor scheduled.

TR-Z07 controller was offline so I went ahead and power cycled the TCU at the zone cabinet. It came back up and tracked normally through the afternoon. No obvious reason for it dropping out in the first place.
KVP36-1743D-0233 would not start at all, and I went ahead and had a look at it, the gate driver had failed which I replaced from the site spares and it fired up fine after that.
mow crew b05, reminded re home runs
Tracker fault on TR-B07-R053. No fault present when I got there, the row was tracking along with the rest of the block. Reset the flag and watched it through a move.
TR-B07-R055 squealing, grease separated, cleaned and repacked. These older rows are all about due.
CB-B02-21 string 13 reading zero per SCADA. Blown fuse, replaced it and the current came back. Nothing else in the can.

Went out and flew the drone over B05 for the IR survey and got the whole block done in the one flight. Two open strings turned up in the imagery which have been ticketed separately for somebody to go and look at, and the rest of the block came back looking normal enough. It was a still morning which made the flying easy.
Eight broken modules in B08, replaced from spares. Rock strike off the mower deck by the look of them.
ces40-1833c-0169 gf, walked strings, nothing found, meggered ok, reset held. 4.3.0 loaded, came back clean
mgx33-1745d-0408 warranty swap done. took two trips, first part turned up damaged in shipping so had to wait on the second

Got called out to an outage on B01 and went out to it. There was a snake got itself across the bus in the skid which was the end of both of them. Cleaned all that up and replaced what was damaged in there. Somebody wants to look at the door seal at the bottom of that skid, there is a gap you could get a hand through.
annual cb inspection cb-b07-19. lugs torqued, ir scan came back clean, no hot spots anywhere in the can

Storm walkdown on B05 following the weather Tuesday. Walked the full block. Found a small number of modules with cracked glass, four in total, all in the outer row facing the prevailing wind. Tagged and photographed each. No racking damage, no wiring pulled down, nothing else out of place. Torque spot checked in the affected row, within spec.

Walkdown of B03 completed. Nothing significant found anywhere in the block, no structural issues and nothing displaced. Two modules with cracked glass noted and added to the punch list for the next replacement round. Nothing else to report.

Slew drive on TR-Z01 was notchy under load when I ran it through the sweep, so I went ahead and regreased it and the old grease had gone hard and separated out same as the others on that block have been doing. The backlash still measures within spec on it so I am leaving it as it is for now rather than changing the drive out. These are all coming up to that age together by the look of it.
TR-B03-R014 stuck at 60 degrees. Motor drawing high current, replaced it.

KVP24-1920B-0360 PM completed. Filters were loaded and were replaced. Fan bank tested, all six running at full speed with no bearing noise on any of them. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors inspected, no pitting. DC bus torque check completed. Unit returned to service reporting normally. Nothing outstanding on this one.
Cleaned the soiling station on MET-03 and wiped the reference cell down. The data had looked stuck so I power cycled the logger while I was there and the values started moving again.
Burned connector on a home run in B04. Cut back and reterminated. String current verified after.

Did the PM on TR-Z01, greased the bearings all the way down the zone and checked the damper bolts as part of it, a couple were loose and got retorqued, same as last time on this one, the ground down the east side is getting soft again and the truck was struggling in places
tracker fault tr-z04, nothing there, reset flag

Submitted the warranty claim on TR-Z02, the drive was inside the coverage window. Serial photographs and the fault description have gone up with the claim. The OEM want the old unit back so it is boxed and staged at the shop. Claim number is in the file.
rtu locked, rebooted, points back
Mowing on B02. Growth was ahead of schedule after the rain and it took the crew an extra day to get through the block properly. Crew signed out at the end of the second day.
SLT25-1909A-0554 PM. Heat sink cleaned, firmware checked, no faults in the log. tbd on the next interval.

Mowing on B04. Growth was well ahead of schedule after the rain and the crew needed an extra day to get through the block properly. Walked behind them afterward on the rows nearest the home run trench and there is no damage to any cabling. Two rows on the south end were left, ground too soft to take the machine. Crew signed out at the end of the second day.

Mow crew on site for B05. Reminded them about the home runs sitting low in the rows before they started. Walked the two rows nearest the home run trench behind them afterward and there is no damage to any of the cabling. Crew signed out at the end of the day.

TR-B01-R066 was not following the rest of the block. Controller reset did not take so the tracker motor was replaced. Row tracking again, verified through two full moves. The old motor was drawing high current on test which is consistent with the failure. Nothing else noted on the row.
MET-04 irradiance reading flatlined so I went out and had a look at it, the sensor had failed outright so I swapped it for a new one and the readings came straight back where they should be
Ground fault on MGX33-1806A-0094. Walked the strings, nothing obvious. Meggered ok, reset held.
Grid fault ride through event took MGX33-2136C-0220 offline. It had cleared on its own before I arrived. Verified the output normal against the neighbours. No action.
TR-B04-R055 lubrication and fastener check done, nothing unusual found on the row at all, everything as it should be

SLT25-1812A-0288 had gone offline so I went out and reset it at the disconnect and it came back up without any trouble at all. There was nothing obviously wrong with it while I was there and it has been reporting fine since.
GF continuity testing B02. All readings within range.
TR-B04-R034 out of alignment, limits recalibrated
mgx33-2001a-0142 high cab temp, filters blocked, cleaned
tr-z04 not following, controller reset didnt take, swapped the gearbox

Pulled thirteen modules from B02 for the warranty claim. Each one photographed front and back and the serial recorded against the claim schedule before removal. All thirteen came from the two rows flagged in the EL imagery last month. Boxed and staged on a pallet at the shop for collection. Strings made up with spares so the block is back to full output, string current verified within about 2 percent of the adjacent strings.
cb-b07-05 low current, water in the enclosure, drained, gland resealed, one fuse
Mow crew on site for B06. Reminded them about the home runs sitting low in the rows before they started.

KVP36-1808A-0338 threw a DC ground fault alarm and I went out and isolated it down to CB-B02-13 where there was a home run chafed against the rack. Repaired it and got it resecured clear. Firmware on this one is 4.4.1 which matches the rest of the block.
b01 wash done, up close to 5% on the reference
Feeder relay tripped on B03. Found a failed termination in the switchgear which had let go. Replaced it and back in service.

The wind sensor on MET-01 was reading zero when there was obviously wind out there. Bearing had gone in the anemometer. Swapped it out for a new one and the readings came straight back where they should be.
Reworked the sagging home runs in B10 before mowing gets there. Spans resecured and clipped clear.
Mow crew on site for B07. Reminded them about the home runs sitting low in the rows before they got started on it.
Regreased the drive on TR-B04-R065. Third one in this block this quarter. Normal wear for the vintage.

CB-B05-22 PM. Found dust ingress coming through the lower gland, enough to leave a film in the base of the enclosure though nothing on the terminations themselves. Cleaned it out and resealed the gland with fresh sealant, torqued the entry. Fuses all checked good and the string currents balanced. The adjacent cans on this row are the same vintage and worth checking for the same thing.
Wrong site.
Ground fault on KVP36-1645D-0114. Walked the strings, nothing obvious anywhere. Meggered ok. Reset and it held.
TR-B01-R093 lubrication and fastener check completed. Nothing unusual found on the row.
CB-B04-20 PM. Found dust ingress coming through the lower gland, cleaned it out and resealed it. Fuses all good, currents balanced. Came back after lunch to check the seal had gone off properly.
Site trip overnight. Relay targets pointed at the main feeder. Walked the collector, nothing visible. Restored under supervision.
TR-B04-R095 squealing, grease separated, cleaned and repacked
comms alarm, all online when i got there, historian gap only

KVP36-1648D-0253 DC GROUND FAULT alarm. Isolated it down to CB-B03-24 where there was a home run chafed through on the rack. Repaired the conductor and got it resecured clear of the steel. Invertor back in service.

Slew drive on TR-Z06 was notchy under load when I ran it through the sweep, so I regreased it and the old grease had gone hard and separated same as the others on that block, the backlash still measures within spec so I am leaving it as it is for now rather than changing the drive out, these are all coming up to that age together
TR-Z01 out of alignment; limits recalibrated; tracking
TR-Z08 comm fault at the zone controller. Reseated the daisy chain, cleared.
Washing crew completed B08 today. Ag dust was heavy on the lower rows, heavier than the last cycle. Crew off site by mid afternoon per the sign out.
Swapped SLT25-2044D-0549 out for a spare from the shop, the old one is boxed up for the RMA, replacement came online and is reporting normally, straightforward enough job

CES40-2028C-0342 tripped on DC GF. Traced it to a pinched connector in CB-B03-18. Replaced the connector and the invertor came back online. It has held since. No pattern in the log going back on this one.
cb-b06-19 low current, water in the enclosure, drained, gland resealed, one fuse
KVP36-1904A-0185 hard fault. Replaced DC contactor. Back online.
Soiling assessment on B04. Soiling ratio around 8% on the ref cells which is well up on the last one. Recommending this block goes in the next wash cycle rather than waiting.

TR-B01-R002 drive replaced. The old grease had hardened right up and the gear faces were scored where it had been running dry. Row back in service and tracking with the block. That is another one off this vintage.
Ground fault on MGX33-1928C-0363. Walked the strings, nothing obvious. Meggered ok, reset and it held.

MGX33-2123B-0196 flagged a fan fault so I went out to have a look at it, and there was a bird nest built up in the intake plenum which I cleared out, a good sized one. The fans were fine once it was clear and the cabinet temperature came back down. There was a gate open on the way in that should not have been which I mentioned to the site lead. Somebody wants to look at the screens on those intakes.
Five broken modules in B06, replaced from spares. Rock strike off the mower deck by the look of it.

Did the torque audit on B02 and sampled ten rack bolts across the block, every one of them came back within tolerance so there was nothing needing doing on it, same as the last one on this block really
B07 walkdown. Nothing significant. Two cracked glass on the punch list.
MGX33-1742D-0351 would not start; DC bus capacitor had failed; rplcd from site spares
Washing crew completed B06. Ag dust was heavy on the lower rows before they started. Crew signed out mid afternoon.

Oil sample pulled from XFMR-B10 and shipped off for DGA. Bushings look fine visually, no weeping or tracking anywhere on them. Results should be back in about two weeks. Nothing else noted on the unit.
wash crew done B08
TR-B03-R043 lubrication and fastener check completed. Nothing unusual found anywhere on the row, all fasteners within spec on the sample.

MGX33-2013A-0367 tripped on DC GF. Traced the fault to a pinched connector in CB-B08-06 where the home run enters the can, the connector body had been trapped against the gland plate on install. Replaced the connector and dressed the run properly clear of the plate. Insulation resistance verified normal on the affected string before restoration. Unit back online and has held. Worth checking the other entries in this can at the next PM, they were all done by the same crew.
MGX33-2140D-0121 AC overcurrent trip. Reset, ran fine rest of the day. No pattern.
Tracker fault on TR-B05-R032. No fault when I got there, everything tracking. Reset the flag.
opened in error

CB-B04-01 low current alarm. There was water in the bottom of the enclosure which I drained out, and resealed the gland where it was getting in. One fuse had gone and was replaced. Currents balanced after.
Washing crew done B06. Ag dust heavy on the lower rows.
comms alarm; all online when i got there; historian gap only
lost scada on b07. fiber run tested bad between the skid and the block, patched around it on the spare pair, needs a permanent fix scheduling
oil sample xfmr-b01 / dga / bushings ok
Wrong site, closing.
Washed B01. Dust heavy on the lower rows. Output up close to 5% next clear day on the ref cells and holding.
Quarterly site walk B08. Cable sag on the north rows, will schedule the rework before the mow crew comes through.
lost scada b07 / fiber bad / patched around / needs proper fix
washed b06, up abt 5%
rtu locked up overnight; rebooted; points came back; no production impact
brush clearing B02 / heavier than last cycle
Reworked the sagging home runs in B05 before mowing gets there. About eight spans resecured and clipped clear. Most of the failures are at the clip fixing rather than the cable pulling through.
Reworked the sagging home runs in B06 before mowing gets there. Spans clipped back up clear.
kvp24-1920b-0360 in warranty, case opened, waiting on rma
MGX33-2140D-0121 high cabinet temp. Filters completely blocked. Cleaned, temp came down.
KVP36-1631C-0337 AC OVERCURRENT trip. Reset the invertor, ran fine the rest of the day. No pattern in the fault log going back.

got called out after the storm came through, there was water in two of the combiner skids over in b08 which i isolated and got pumped out. both dried out and back in service now. the road down that side was a mess and it took a while to get there at all

The wind sensor on MET-01 was reading zero when there was obviously wind out there, you could hear it going through the racking. Bearing had gone in the anemometer so I swapped it out for a new one and the readings came straight back where they should be. Second one of these this year.

CES40-1813A-0278 cooling alarm. One fan seized on the bank, replaced it from spares. Remaining five tested and all running at full speed. Cabinet temperature came back into normal range within the hour. Filters were clean.
Swapped SLT25-1740D-0930 out for a spare. Old one going back on the RMA.
soiling assessment b05, ratio abt 2% on the ref cells, recommending wash next cycle

Went out to look at SLT25-2038C-0718 which had thrown a comms fault. There is nothing actually wrong with the unit itself as far as I can tell, it was inverting away quite happily the whole time and the meter agrees. Reset the comms card and it started reporting again. These seem to do this now and then.

Had the vendor on the phone for the diagnostics on MGX33-2022B-0245. Ended up replacing the AC contactor. Verified the AC output balanced across all three phases on restart and the DC bus at 1044 V, both normal. Unit has run through to end of shift with no faults. Took most of the day, largely waiting on their support queue. Old contactor is boxed for return. Ruled out the gate drivers and the cooling system before we went to the contactor, both tested fine.

Went out and did the fence and gate check, and the lens on camera 3 was fogged up again so I wiped it down and got it looking clear from the control room. The rest of the perimeter looked sound the whole way round with no breaches or washouts anywhere on it.
Row TR-B05-R025 out of alignment with the block. Recalibrated the limits, tracking normal now.
SLT25-1828C-0434 not reporting / reseated comms module + RS485 / fine
B02 walkdown. 2 cracked glass for punch list.
string out b09; shattered cells; swapped
ces40-2035c-0307 pm; sinks; contactors ok
TR-B03-R090 tracker PM. Bearings greased, damper bolts checked, two were loose and retorqued. Nothing else out of order on the row.
TR-Z02 stuck at -45 degrees. Motor high current, replaced it. Tracking again.
Cable management repair in B05. Wire runs had dropped down into the mow path. Resecured about eleven spans and clipped them clear.
Annual inspection on CB-B01-17. Lugs torqued while I had it open and the IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere in the can.
TR-B01-R060; no fault present; tracking; flag reset
Twelve broken modules in B01, replaced from spares. Rock strike off the mower deck.
mgx33-1946d-0341 down on ac undervolt, poi normal, reset and monitored two hours
TR-B02-R078 drive replaced. Grease hardened, gear faces scored.
Fence and gate check completed. The lens on camera 3 was fogged so I wiped it down. Rest of the perimeter is sound.
lost scada b04 / fiber bad skid to block / patched around / needs permanent fix

Pulled six modules from B09 for the warranty claim. Each photographed front and back before removal, serial numbers recorded against the claim schedule. All six came from the row flagged in the EL imagery. Boxed and staged at the shop for collection. Strings made up with spares, string current verified back within 2 percent of the adjacent strings. Photos and serial list are in the claim file.

TR-Z08 was squealing on the east sweep, same as the others on that block have been doing, and the old grease had separated out and gone hard so I cleaned it all out and repacked it properly. These older rows are all coming up to that age together and it is not really a surprise on this vintage.

somebody had a go at the fence over at b02 and taken some of the grounding conductor. filed the report with the sheriff and got the fence patched the same day, conductor has been replaced. camera on that corner is pointed the wrong way

Trimmed the tree line along the east boundary again, same as last year, it was starting to shade the first two rows through the morning and you could see it in the string data if you looked, cut it back well past the fence this time so hopefully we get more than one season out of it, brush is piled at the north gate for the chipper
Scheduled wash on B04 completed and the crew got finished ahead of the wind advisory that came in that afternoon. I walked a couple of rows behind them to check the coverage and it looked good.
3 modules broken b02, rplcd
Went out and did the post emergent on B07, spot treating along the fence line where the growth comes through worst, and the records are written up in the binder
Oil sample pulled from XFMR-B05 and shipped for DGA. Bushings visually ok, no weeping.
5 broken modules B01 / rplcd from spares / rock strike off the mower

KVP24-1617B-0122 showed a grid fault ride through event at 1412 per the HMI. Unit had already cleared and resynced before I arrived on site. Output verified normal against the neighbouring units. No action taken.

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO on the string before starting. Burned connector on one of the home runs in B01, cut it back well past the damaged section and reterminated it. Verified the string current came back afterward. Permit closed at the end of the job.
TR-Z03 tracker PM. Bearings greased and the damper bolts checked as part of it, two were loose so they got retorqued. Came back after lunch to finish the far end.
Lightning took out the comms and a surge card overnight. Partial monitoring restored, rest tomorrow.
Combiner PM on CB-B01-10. IR scan showed nothing in the can. String currents balanced per SCADA. Lugs torqued.
Washing crew completed B07. Ag dust was heavy on the lower rows before they started. Crew signed out mid afternoon.

Semiannual PM on KVP24-1917B-0308. Filters replaced and the cabinet vacuumed out, and the torque check on the DC bus was done with everything within spec. Nothing came up on it. Temperture in the skid was up but not unusual.
CX-R14 inspection done, checked over the coolant loop and the door seals and it was all fine, no alarms showing on the rack at all
B01 wash done. Crew started at the west end. Next clear day the block was up close to 5% on the reference, about what we expected.
TR-Z04 drive replaced, grease hardened, gear faces scored. Row back in service.
Storm callout / water in 2 combiner skids B02 / isolated / pumped out

Slew drive on TR-B05-R071 was notchy under load when I ran it through. Regreased it, the old grease had gone stiff. Backlash still measures within spec so leaving it as is for now. tbd whether it needs the drive changed at the next round.
MGX33-2135C-0106 DC ground fault alarm. Isolated to CB-B08-11, found a chafed home run against the rack. Repaired and returned to service.
Called out after the storm. Water in two of the combiner skids in B07, isolated both and pumped them out per the HMI alarms.
kvp24-1542d-0324 dc gf, cb-b01-09, chafed home run, repaired
Grid fault ride through event took KVP24-1601A-0334 offline. It had cleared on its own before I arrived on site. Verified output normal against the neighbouring units per SCADA. No action required.

Had the vendor on the phone walking me through the diagnostics on KVP24-1620B-0309 and it took most of the day between the hold times and getting the cabinet apart. It came down to the DC contactor in the end which we swapped out and it came back up fine.
Burned connector on a home run in B05. Cut it back well past the damaged section and reterminated. String current verified back to normal afterward. The connector body had discoloured badly.

CES40-2206A-0333 cooling alarm. One fan seized on the bank, replaced it from spares. Remaining five tested and all running at full speed. Cabinet temperature came back into normal range within the hour.

TR-B07-R026 was stuck flat at 0 degrees when I got out there to it. The motor was pulling high current on the meter which is generally what it turns out to be with these. Replaced it and the row is tracking again with the rest of the block now. Verified it through a full sweep before I left site. Nothing else on the row worth reporting.
met-03 wind sensor zero, bearing gone, swapped

Was up at B02 doing the module clamp torque sweep today, the drive up was fine, gate was open when I got there which it should not have been so I mentioned it to the site lead, anyway there was a run of loose clamps along the east rows which I retorqued, the rest of what I sampled was fine, and the fence on the north side needs looking at
CB-B09-01 annual inspection. Lugs torqued, IR scan clean, no hot spots in the can.
KVP24-1643D-0303 semiannual. Filters replaced, cabinet vacuumed, DC bus torque check done. No issues.
TR-Z07 PM; bearings greased; 2 damper bolts loose
B08 site walk. Cable sag on the north rows, will schedule.
kvp36-2419b-0361 derating all afternoon, down maybe 12% on its neighbours, no fault logged
TR-B01-R030 comm fault at zone ctrl / reseated daisy chain / cleared

Quarterly torque check on the module clamps in B03. Twelve came back below spec and were retorqued to 18 Nm. The rest of what I sampled across the block was all within tolerance. It was cold enough that the wrench was slow to click.
CB-B02-22 PM. Found dust ingress coming through the lower gland, cleaned it out and resealed. Fuses all good, currents balanced per SCADA.

Grid fault ride through event took KVP36-2423B-0265 offline. It had cleared on its own and resynced before I arrived on site. Verified the output was normal against the neighbouring units per SCADA. No action required.
Did the combiner PM on CB-B01-09, IR scan showed nothing in the can at all and the string currents were balanced per SCADA, lugs torqued while I was in there, nothing much else to say about it
cb-b09-23 + adjacent, megger normal

Went out to a string that was out over in B07 and had a look at it, there was one module with the cells shattered up in the corner, glass still whole but the cells are gone, swapped it out from spares and the string came back up to where it should be
sched wash b08 done, ahead of the wind advisory
String out in B06. Found one module with a shattered cell area, glass intact but the cells are gone. Swapped it from spares. String current back to normal.
TR-Z06 PM. Bearings greased, two damper bolts loose, retorqued.

Grid fault ride through event took KVP24-1623B-0353 offline at about 1355 per the HMI. The unit had cleared the fault and resynced on its own before I arrived on site. Verified the output was normal against the neighbouring units, all reading consistently. No action required on it.

Seven broken modules in B04, all replaced from spares. The damage pattern on all of them is consistent with rock strike from the mower deck rather than anything else: impact points on the lower third, glass starred outward. Torqued and re-strung, string current verified back to normal against the adjacent strings. Recommend the mow crew fit the deflectors that were specified for this site, this is the fourth incident of the same kind.
MET-03 pyranometers and rain gauge cleaned. RSR releveled, the bubble was well off.
Walked B01 for soiling. Dust accumulation moderate. Not washing yet.

Got a call that half the string inverters over in B06 had gone offline overnight, so I went ahead and drove out first thing to have a look. By the time I got there every one of them was back up and reporting normally, nothing to do. It had been a very humid night, the fog was still sitting in the low ground when I came through the gate, and these do seem to do it when it is like that. No production loss at all, they were inverting the whole time as far as the meter is concerned, it is just the reporting that drops.

Pulled the permit before going out to SLT25-1940D-0809 which had dropped off the network again. It is the same story as every other time with these units, by the time I got out there and had the LOTO sorted out it had already come back on its own after a power cycle at the AC disconnect. Production was never affected at any point, the meter shows it inverting the whole way through, it is purely the reporting that drops out and then recovers on its own. Logged it and closed the permit.
perimeter walk / fence ok / washout south gate filled

SLT25-2129C-0139 is showing offline in the portal but it is generating away perfectly normally per the meter, same as the rest of them on that row seem to do. The firmware on the comms board is a couple of revs back from current so I have gone ahead and flagged that for the next update window rather than doing anything about it today.
KVP24-1610A-0147. Vendor diagnostics on the phone. DC bus capacitor swapped. All day job.

Burned connector on a home run in B07. Cut back well past the damaged section and reterminated. Verified the string current returned to match the adjacent strings. The connector body had discoloured and the insulation was brittle either side of it, consistent with a poor crimp rather than external damage.
TR-B10-R094 stuck at 25 degrees. Motor high current, replaced it. Tracking again.

CES40-2203A-0144 threw a DC ground fault alarm so I went out and isolated it down to CB-B09-17 where there was a home run chafed clean through against the rack upright, the insulation was worn right down on it. Repaired the run and got it resecured properly clear of the steel this time. The unit is back in service and it has held since. That is the second one like it on this block and I would say it is worth somebody walking the rest of the runs down there rather than waiting for the next one to go.
Torque audit B04. Sampled seven rack bolts, all within tolerance. No retorquing needed.
cabinet temp alarm on kvp36-2423b-0265, reading high but under the trip point; nothing obviously wrong inside; left it running
scada showed kvp36-2422b-0178 offline, drove out expecting comms, unit was in fault and had stopped itself, restarted
tr-z06 annual, slew greased, backlash ok

Pre emergent application on B02. Started at the north end with wind at approximately 6 mph, within label. Wind picked up through the morning and by lunch was sustained above the label limit on the exposed west edge, so held off on that strip and completed the remainder. Approximately 75 percent of the block treated. Buffer maintained at the drainage throughout. Remainder scheduled for the next suitable morning.
LIGHTNING overnight took out the comms and a surge card. Got partial monitoring restored, the rest tomorrow when the card comes in.
Washing crew completed B09. Ag dust heavy on the lower rows.
Ground fault continuity testing B09. All readings within range, nothing to report.
Washed B01. Dust was heavy on the lower rows. Checked the strings against the ref cells the next clear day, output up close to 5% and holding.
scada showed kvp36-2419b-0365 offline, drove out expecting comms, unit was in fault and had stopped itself. restarted, back online. fw 4.2.1 on this one

KVP36-2426B-0296 tripped on AC overcurrent and I went out and had a look at it. Reset the unit and it ran fine for the rest of the day without any further trouble. Had a look back through the fault log and there is nothing that I would call a pattern in there. Nothing much else to say about this one, it has been fine since.
ces40-1844d-0183 pm, sinks, contactors ok
Mowing on B02 complete. Two rows on the south end were skipped, the ground is too soft to take the machine safely. Those will be picked up on the next pass once it firms up. No damage to any cabling.

Module clamp torque sweep on B06. Found a run of loose clamps along the east rows same as the last sweep, retorqued the lot of them to spec. The rest of what I sampled across the block was fine. It is always the east rows on this one.

Went out to a string that was out in B03, and there was one module in it with the cells shattered up in the corner, glass still whole but the cells are gone, swapped it from spares and the string came back up, the road down there is rough and I would guess it is stone off the mower
Finished the mowing on B07 and two rows had to be skipped because the ground was too soft to take the machine down there, they will get picked up on the next pass once it has dried out a bit
Opened in error.
warranty modules in B03, torqued and re-strung
Drone IR flight over B04 completed. Two open strings found in the imagery and ticketed separately. Rest of the block looked normal.

Quarterly site walk on B01. Cable sag noted on the north rows, roughly a dozen spans hanging low enough to be at risk when the mow crew comes through. Checked the clips on the affected spans and several have failed at the fixing rather than the cable having pulled through. Rest of the block is fine. Recommend the rework uses the heavier clip.
7 modules broken B04, rplcd from spares
Quarterly site walk B02. Cable sag on the north rows, will schedule the rework.
TR-Z09 lubrication and fastener check completed. Nothing unusual found anywhere on the zone. All rows tracking normally. tbd on the next interval.

Site tripped overnight. Relay targets pointed at the main feeder. Walked the whole collector run and the switchgear in daylight, nothing visible anywhere. Restored under supervision. No root cause found.
Two fuses out in CB-B07-24, replaced both. Checked for a cause and found nothing at all in the can.
PM on KVP36-1640D-0368. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors checked for pitting and none found. Logged and closed out.
smoke reported b01 skid, no fire on arrival, bad discoloration one mv termination, isolated and loto pending engineering
Burned connector on a home run in B03. Cut it back well past the damaged section and reterminated it. String current verified back to normal afterward. The connector body had discoloured badly.
TR-Z08 lubrication and fastener check completed. Nothing unusual found anywhere on the zone. All rows tracking.

Torque audit on B04. Sampled four rack bolts, all within tolerance. That is a thin sample for a block this size and I would suggest the next audit takes a dozen or more spread across the rows rather than four.

Oil sample pulled from XFMR-B02 and shipped for DGA. Bushings inspected visually from ground level, no weeping, no tracking and no compound migration on any of them. Gas relay checked and clear. LTC counter read and recorded against the previous reading. Results expected inside two weeks.
grid fault ride thru took kvp36-2422b-0175 offline. cleared on its own before i got there. output verified normal
Scheduled wash on B01 completed. Crew finished ahead of the wind advisory that came in that afternoon.
Mowed B02. Growth was well ahead of schedule after the rain we had, took an extra day to get through it properly. Crew back next cycle. tbd whether we shorten the interval on this block.

TR-Z04 tracker PM. Bearings greased across the zone and the damper bolts checked as part of it, two were found loose and were retorqued to spec. Nothing else out of order on any row. Zone handed back tracking.
Quarterly site walk on B05. Cable sag noted on the north rows which will need scheduling before the mow crew comes back through. Rest of the block looked to be in reasonable order per the walk.
met-04 irradiance flatlined, sensor failed, swapped

Grid fault ride through event took MGX33-1644D-0331 offline at approximately 1340. The unit had cleared the fault and resynchronised on its own before I arrived on site. Verified output normal against the two neighbouring units, all three within about 1 percent of each other on the same irradiance. Pulled the event record from the unit: undervoltage on two phases lasting roughly 180 ms, which is consistent with a transmission side event rather than anything on the plant. No action required, nothing to fix.
B01 storm walkdown. Few cracked glass, tagged. Rest fine.
sched wash b08 done, ahead of the wind advisory

Went out to CB-B01-12 on the low current alarm and dealt with it, there was some water in the bottom of the enclosure which I got out and the gland has been resealed so that should hold now. One of the fuses had gone as well and that has been replaced. Everything looked alright by the time I left it and the currents were reading where they should be, so it is all sorted on this one as far as I am concerned.
TR-Z06 was stuck out at -45 degrees when I got to it. The motor was pulling high current on the meter so it was replaced and the row is tracking again with the block. tbd on the old one.
Drone flight over B01 completed this morning. Two open strings found in the imagery, both ticketed separately. Rest of the block looked normal.
tr-z09 annual svc, greased the slew drive, backlash within spec
Walkdown of B10 completed. Nothing significant to report from the block. Two modules with cracked glass noted and added to the punch list for the next replacement round.

Comms alarm came in overnight but everything was already back online and reporting normally by the time I got out there. There is a gap in the historian but no production impact from any of it at all as far as I can tell.

Went out and did the PM on MGX33-2146D-0148 and got everything on the sheet done for it. The filters were pretty well loaded so they were swapped out for a fresh set, and the fan bank was tested with all six of them running as they should be, no noise off any of them. Nothing else came up needing following. The unit was reporting normally when I closed it up and left it.
mowed b04, growth ahead of schedule, extra day
Went out and cleaned the pyranometers and the rain gauge on MET-04 and got the RSR releveled while I was up the mast, the bubble had drifted a fair way off which it always does at that one

MGX33-2021B-0327 threw a DC ground fault alarm. Isolated the fault down to CB-B04-05 where I found a home run chafed through against the rack upright, the insulation worn right down to the conductor. Repaired the run and resecured it clear of the steel with a proper standoff rather than the tie it had been fixed with. Insulation resistance verified normal on the affected string before restoration. Unit returned to service and the fault has not recurred. The remaining runs in this can are fixed the same way and are worth checking at the next PM.
Copper theft attempt at B02. Fence cut and some grounding conductor taken. Report filed, repaired the same day.
Twelve broken modules in B08, replaced from spares. Rock strike off the mower deck by the look of them.
Module wash on B05 with the two truck crew and deionized water. Output up about 6 percent on the next clear day per SCADA. Crew off site mid afternoon.

CES40-2023B-0392 tripped on AC overcurrent per the HMI. Reset the unit and it ran fine for the remainder of the day. Reviewed the fault log back twelve months and there is no pattern: this is the only overcurrent event recorded on this unit. POI voltage and frequency traces for the time of the trip look normal. Ruled out a plant side cause. Nothing to action, unit left in service and monitored.
Grass fire along the south fence, the FD handled it. Checked the array over, no damage to any of the modules.
B07 clamp check; 13 below spec; retorqued to 18 Nm

Semiannual PM on CES40-2115B-0226. Filters replaced, cabinet vacuumed out and the DC bus torque check completed, all connections within spec. Fan bank tested, all six running at full speed with no bearing noise on any of them. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors inspected and no pitting found anywhere. Cabinet temperature at end of PM reading 41 C against an ambient of 33, which is normal for this unit and this position. No faults in the log since the last visit. Running 4.3.0, flagged for the next update window. Nothing outstanding.

POI breaker tripped in the early hours and took the whole plant down with it, and I got out there as quick as I could to have a look round. As it turned out the utility said it was on their side of the interconnect so there was not a great deal for me to be doing about it. It took them a good while to get it sorted out at their end, we were off for something like seven hours all told before it came back on. Nothing wrong on our equipment anywhere as far as I could see when I walked the collector and the switchgear.

Did the annual inspection on CB-B09-05 and went ahead and torqued all the lugs while I was in there, the IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere in the can. There was a bull snake curled up under the skid steps which took some persuading to move along before I could get in.

Got the call about the B03 units showing offline in the portal again. Went out and had a look at them but by the time I was standing in front of the cabinets they were all reporting fine, which is more or less what happened last time and the time before. Nothing to action as far as I can see, they seem to sort themselves out on their own. Logged it so there is a record.
twelve broken modules in b03, rplcd from spares. rock strike off the mower deck by the look of them
Went out and did the torque audit on B04 and sampled five rack bolts across the block, and all of them came back within tolerance so nothing needed doing on it, quiet enough morning out there
Walkdown of B10. Nothing significant. Two cracked modules noted for the punch list.
ces40-2041d-0107 down on ac undervolt, poi ok, reset

CES40-2213A-0368 was down on AC undervoltage when I got out to it and I had a look at the POI first which was reading normal enough, so there was nothing wrong on that side of it at all. Reset the unit and monitored it for a couple of hours before I left and there were no further trips off it.
KVP24-1922B-0159 flagged a fan fault. Bird nest in the intake plenum, cleared it out. Fans fine after.
Finished the mowing on B05, two rows on the south end had to be left because the ground is still too soft to take the machine down there safely, they will get picked up on the next pass
Opened a warranty case on KVP24-1923B-0166. OEM want the fault logs before they authorise anything, sent them over.
Torque audit on B02. Sampled eleven rack bolts, all within tolerance.

Pre emergent application on B03. Started at the north end with wind at approximately 5 mph. Wind picked up after lunch to a sustained 13 mph with gusts above that, which is over the label limit, so held off on the west edge at that point. Approximately 70 percent of the block treated. Remainder scheduled for tomorrow morning. Buffer maintained at the drainage throughout.
post emergent b08, fence line spot treated, records in binder

Went out and did the GF testing on CB-B06-05 and the cans either side of it, and all the megger readings came back normal across every string I tested, there was nothing outside the expected range anywhere so nothing to report from any of them
SLT25-1823B-0416 offline. Reset it at the disconnect and it came back up fine.

Went out with the wash crew for B09, two truck setup with the deionized water same as usual, and they got through the whole block in the day which was better than I expected given how it looked when we started. Output came back up about 4 percent on the next clear day per SCADA. There is not much more to say about it really, it all went as it should have and the crew were off site by five.
string out b06, module with shattered cells, swapped it from spares
rtu locked overnight, rebooted, points back

Went ahead and did the module clamp torque sweep on B02 and there was a run of loose clamps along the east rows which I retorqued, same as the last time I did this block. The rest of what I sampled was all fine. There was a family of foxes denning under the end of one of the rows which I left well alone. It is always the east side on this one and I would guess that is the wind loading.
Quarterly site walk B01. Some cable sag on the north rows which will need scheduling. Rest of the block looked fine.
Outage on B06. Found a snake across the bus in the skid. Cleaned up and replaced what was damaged in there.

Did the PM on KVP24-1605A-0266 today, cleaned the heat sinks off and checked the contactors for any pitting which there was none of, same as the last one I did on that row, got it logged and closed out before the afternoon
Replaced the TR-B06-R013 motor under warranty. Paperwork and the serial photos have been uploaded to the claim file.
cable mgmt B07 / 13 spans resecured
TR-B03-R044 stuck at 52 / motor high current / rplcd

Two broken modules in B03, both replaced from spares. The damage pattern on both is consistent with rock strike from the mower deck: impact point on the lower third with the glass starred outward from it. Torqued and re-strung, string current verified back to normal against the adjacent strings. This is the third incident of this kind on this block and the deflectors specified for the mow deck are still not fitted.
Same units in B03 dropping out again. Logged it, no action taken, they come back on their own every time. No production lost.

Walkdown of B09 completed. Nothing significant found in the block, no structural issues and nothing displaced. Two modules with cracked glass noted and added to the punch list for the next replacement round.
Pulled the oil sample off XFMR-B01 and got it shipped for the DGA. The bushings all look alright from the ground with no weeping or tracking on any of them. Results back in a couple of weeks.
gf testing cb-b07-23 and adjacent, megger normal
TR-B04-R090 squealing, grease separated, cleaned and repacked
Ground fault on KVP24-1912A-0220. Walked the strings, nothing obvious. Meggered ok, reset and it held.

TR-Z01 zone controller was showing offline. Power cycled the TCU at the zone cabinet and it came back up immediately. Verified the zone tracked through two full moves afterward with all rows in agreement within about half a degree. No fault stored in the controller log, so no root cause established for the dropout.

Went out and did the PM on KVP24-2413A-0151 and got everything on the sheet done. The heat sinks were cleaned off and the contacters checked over for pitting, none found on any of them. Logged and closed out. Hot as hell in that skid.

KVP36-1634C-0221 flagged a fan fault. Opened the cabinet and found a bird nest built up in the intake plenum, a good sized one. Cleared it out and the fans were running properly again after that, cabinet temperature back to normal within the hour. The intake screens on this unit are damaged which is how it got in, recommend they are replaced rather than just clearing the nest.
Two broken modules in B02, replaced from spares. Damage looks like rock strike off the mower deck. Mow crew have been told again.
tr-z01 pm, greased, 2 damper bolts loose

Module clamp torque sweep completed on B05. Found a run of clamps below specification concentrated on the east rows, twenty two in total, all retorqued to 18 Nm. Sampled a further forty five across the remaining rows, all within tolerance. The east rows take the afternoon wind loading at this site, which is consistent with the pattern. No module or glass damage associated with the loose clamps.

Went out to CB-B02-13 on a low current alarm and it was the same story as the others on that row, there was water sat in the bottom of the enclosure which I drained out and the gland has been resealed, one fuse had gone and that was replaced. Currents were back where they should be by the time I left. That is three cans on that row now with the same problem and I have said before that somebody should look at the whole lot rather than waiting for them to alarm one at a time.
Installed the warranty modules in B06. Torqued and re-strung, string current back to normal against the adjacent strings. Old ones staged for collection.
Storm walkdown on B03. Few modules with cracked glass, tagged them. Everything else looked fine.
Grid fault ride through event took MGX33-2132C-0348 offline. It had cleared on its own before I arrived. Verified output normal against the neighbours.

Ground fault came up on MGX33-2144D-0221 so I went out and walked all the strings on it looking for a cause. Nothing obvious anywhere, no chafing and no pinched connectors. Meggered the lot and the readings came back fine. Reset it and it has held since.
annual inspection cb-b05-03. lugs torqued, ir scan clean, no hot spots

SLT25-1937C-0312 is showing offline in the portal but it is generating away normally per the meter, same as the others on that row do. The firmware on the comms board is a couple of revs back so I have flagged that for the next update window rather than doing anything today.

Went up for the quarterly site walk on B01 and had a good look round it, there is cable sag on the north rows which will want scheduling before the mow crew comes back through, otherwise the block looked reasonable enough

PM sweep on the string inverters in B05. Cleaned the intakes on five units, all of them well loaded with dust. One had a noisy fan which sounds like a bearing rather than an obstruction, tagged for follow up at the next visit rather than dealing with it today. The permit was pulled and the LOTO done at each unit in turn as I worked along the row, and closed out at the end. Recommend the interval on this block is shortened, these load faster than the units on the north side of the site.
ces40-2040d-0409 pm, filters swapped, fans ok
Comms fault on SLT25-1931C-0995. Nothing wrong with the unit at all, it was inverting fine the whole time it showed offline. Reset the comms card and it started reporting.
perimeter walk; fence ok; washout by south gate filled
Warranty replacement modules installed in B08. Old modules on the pallet for RMA collection. Serials recorded and photographed for the claim file.

Got called out to an outage on B04 and went out to it. There was a snake got across the bus in the skid and that was the end of both of them. Cleaned it all up and replaced what was damaged in there. Not the best job I have had this year. It was back in service before it got light. Somebody wants to look at how it got in there in the first place, the door seal at the bottom is not sitting right at all.

Went out to CB-B01-22 where two fuses were out and replaced them both, and I had a good look round for a cause while I was in there and there was nothing obvious at all to find, no water and nothing chafed anywhere. Currents balanced after.
cb-b01-23 pm, dust in gland, cleaned and resealed, fuses good
tr-z06 not following, reset didnt take, swapped the motor

Sprayed B05 and had to stop early because the wind picked up after lunch and got over the label limit. About two thirds of the block is done. The rest will get finished tomorrow morning if it drops off the way they say it will. Buffer maintained at the drainage.
two fuses out cb-b10-11, rplcd
b01 clamp check, 13 below spec, all retorqued to 18 Nm
wash crew done b08

Went out and did the soiling assessment on B09 and the ratio is reading around 3 percent on the reference cells, which is not far off where it was at the last one. I went ahead and walked the block as well and the accumulation is light and fairly even across it. Recommending it goes in the next wash cycle rather than being brought forward at all. There was a coyote sat watching me from the far fence the whole time.
KVP24-1911A-0271 down on AC undervoltage. POI looked normal on the meters. Reset and monitored two hours.
CES40-2116B-0211 failed to start. Gate driver had failed, replaced from spares.
Regreased the drive on TR-B03-R059. That is the third one in this block this quarter. Normal wear for the vintage on these.

Got called out after the storm came through and there was water in two of the combiner skids over in B04, isolated both of them and got them pumped out. Both are dried out and back in service now. The road down that side was under water in a couple of places so it took a while.

Regreased the drive on TR-B04-R062, that is the third one in this block this quarter now, the old grease had gone hard on it same as the others. Normal wear for the vintage on these and I would say the rest of the block wants doing before they start making a noise about it.
kvp24-2419b-0345 semiannual, filters, vacuum, torque, no issues
b04 soiling ratio abt 8%, recommending wash next cycle
Two fuses out in CB-B05-10, replaced both. Checked for a cause and found nothing.
Walked B06 for soiling. Dust accumulation moderate, not washing yet.
TR-Z08 out of alignment. Recalibrated limits, tracking now.
Wind sensor on MET-02 reading zero when there was obviously wind out there. Bearing had gone in the anemometer, swapped it out and the readings came back.

Comms alarm came in overnight but everything was already back online by the time I got out there. Historian gap only and no production impact from any of it. Chkd the switch and the media converter while I was in the skid, both fine. Nothing to do.
Walkdown of B08 completed. Nothing significant found anywhere in the block. Two modules with cracked glass noted and added to the punch list for the next replacement round.
B07 clamp sweep; loose run east rows; retorqued
TR-B04-R046 drive rplcd, grease hardened
Quarterly site walk on B05. Cable sag noted on the north rows which will want scheduling. Rest of the block fine.
KVP36-1812A-0237 tripped on AC overcurrent per the HMI. Reset the unit and it ran fine for the remainder of the day. No pattern in the fault log going back.
TR-B01-R039 lubrication and fastener check done, nothing unusual anywhere on the row, all of it as it should be
KVP36-2420B-0352 is still under parts warranty so a case was opened with the OEM rather than going ahead with the repair. Waiting on the RMA number now. Unit isolated in the meantime.
Cable management repair in B04. Wire runs had dropped into the mow path, resecured about four spans and clipped them clear.
CB-B01-07 PM. Found dust ingress on the lower gland, cleaned it out and resealed. Fuses all good.

Went out and did the pre emergent on B05 and the wind was borderline through the morning so I held off on the west edge and got the rest of the block done. Will pick that strip up another morning when it drops off a bit. The buffer was maintained at the drainage the whole way along and the records are written up in the binder.
Went ahead and did the annual on XFMR-B09, checked the LTC counter and the gas relay which was clear, and cleaned the bushings down while I was up there.
CES27-1521B-0709 showing isolation fault. Damp morning, cleared once it dried out. tbd if it recurs.
POI breaker tripped and took the plant down. Utility said it was their side. Restored after coordination with them, about four hours off. Nothing on us.
ground fault continuity testing b02, all readings came back within range, nothing to report
warranty case opened on ces40-1528c-0358, oem want the fault logs
MV cable fault between B01 and the collector. The locator put it at about 300 ft in from the block end. Both ends isolated and grounded and tagged out. Contractor scheduled.
MET-03 irradiance flatlined. Sensor failed, swapped it.

Got called out after the storm came through and there was water in two of the combiner skids over in B07 which I isolated and got pumped out. It took me a while to get down there at all because the low crossing was under water and I had to come round through the top gate. Both skids are dried out and back in service now. That is the second time on that row this year and I have said before that the gland seals want looking at properly rather than us doing them one at a time as they alarm.
B05 clamp sweep; loose run east rows; retorqued
CB-B05-01 PM. IR clean, currents balanced.

Went out and did the semiannual on MGX33-1638C-0257, it took a bit longer than usual because of the wind, and got everything done that was on the list, filters, the cabinet vacuum, the torque check on the bus. Nothing came up that I would call an issue. Unit was back online before I left site and reporting normally, so all good from my end on this one.
3 modules B08 flagged for claim
KVP36-2339C-0174 tripped on DC GF, went out and traced it down to a pinched connector in CB-B04-18 which I replaced, and the unit came back online after that and has held since
CB-B09-03 string 5 reading zero on the portal. Blown fuse, replaced it and the current came straight back. Checked the strings either side, both normal.
TR-Z05 lubrication and fastener check completed across the zone. Nothing unusual found on any row, all fasteners within spec on the sample taken. Zone tracking normally.
Soiling station MET-03 cleaned and the reference cell wiped. Data looked stuck so power cycled the logger.

Went out and did the GF testing on CB-B08-13 and the cans either side of it, all the megger readings came back normal across every string I tested so there is nothing at all to report from any of them

Did the PM on TR-B04-R020, greased the bearings and went round the damper bolts, two were loose and got retorqued same as last time on this row, there is a low spot at the north end that holds water and the bearings down there always look worse for it
MGX33-2127C-0310 DC ground fault alarm. Isolated to CB-B05-18 where there was a home run chafed against the rack. Repaired and resecured clear of the steel. Unit back in service.
Mowed B05. Growth ahead of schedule after the rain, took an extra day.

Sprayed B06 and had to stop early because the wind picked up after lunch and got over the label limit, same as happened on B03 a couple of weeks back, will finish the rest of it tomorrow morning if it drops off like they say it will, the buffer at the drainage was maintained the whole way along
GF testing on CB-B03-17 and the cans either side of it. Megger readings all came back normal across every string tested. Nothing outside the expected range, nothing to report from any of them.
MET-04 irradiance flatlined / sensor failed / swapped
vandalism, modules shot out along the road side, documented and rplcd 12

Went out and pulled the oil sample off XFMR-B03 and got it shipped away for the DGA. The bushings all looked to be in reasonable order from the ground with no weeping or tracking on any of them that I could see. It took a while to find the sample kit because somebody had moved it out of the shop and not put it back where it belongs. Results should be back in a couple of weeks.
mgx33-2011a-0312 dc gf, pinched connector cb-b03-07, rplcd
reworked sagging home runs b02 ahead of the mow crew
TR-Z07 drive replaced. The old grease had hardened right up and the gear faces were scored where it had been running dry. Row back in service and tracking with the block.

Three modules from B05 have been flagged for the claim, the serials are recorded and the EL images are attached to the file, they came out of the row that was picked up on the last survey and they are staged at the shop for collection
ces27-1541d-0576 pm, heat sink cleaned, fw chkd, no faults in the log
Pulled the oil sample off XFMR-B05 and got it shipped for the DGA, the bushings all look alright from the ground with no weeping anywhere on them, results should be back in a couple of weeks
TR-B03-R076 was not following the rest of the block. Controller reset did not take so the limit switch was swapped out and the row recalibrated. Tracking again now.
kvp24-1907a-0125 pm, sinks cleaned, contactors ok, closed
CX-R06 HVAC alarm, compressor short cycling. Vendor coming out.
cb-b08-08 annual, lugs, ir clean
TR-B04-R058 was showing a comm fault at the zone controller so I went out and reseated the daisy chain connections and it cleared straight away. Row tracking normally after that.

Went out and did the GF testing on CB-B01-16 and the cans either side of it, and all the megger readings came back normal across every string that I tested with nothing outside the expected range anywhere at all on it
tr-b05-r092 annual, slew greased, backlash ok

Went out and pulled the oil sample off XFMR-B03 and got it shipped away for the DGA. The bushings all looked alright from the ground with no weeping or tracking on any of them. Results back in a couple of weeks.

Coyote had dug under the fence on the north side and chewed clean through one of the home runs in B02, repaired the conductor and got the fence patched up where it had got under, that is getting to be a regular thing along that stretch and somebody should put a proper apron in rather than us going out and patching it every few months like this
CB-B10-06 PM. Found dust ingress on the lower gland, cleaned it out and resealed. Fuses all good.
Perimeter inspection done. Fence intact the whole way round except for the washout near the south gate where the drainage cuts under, filled that in and packed it down.

KVP36-1641D-0098 PM complete. Filters were loaded and were replaced with a fresh set. Fan bank tested, all six running at full speed with no bearing noise on any of them. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors inspected and no pitting found. DC bus torque check completed, all within spec. Cabinet temperature normal at end of PM. Nothing outstanding on this unit.

Ten modules from B03 have been flagged for the claim, the serials are all recorded and the EL images are attached to the file, they came out of the row that was picked up on the last survey and are staged at the shop for collection

MGX33-1644D-0325 tripped on AC overcurrent, reset it and it ran fine the rest of the day, same as the one over in B02 did a few weeks back, there is no pattern in the log that I can see going back through the year
Ten broken modules in B07, replaced from spares. Rock strike off the mower deck.
CB-B02-05 string 14 zero. Blown fuse, rplcd.
Went ahead and did the ground fault continuity testing on B05 and all the readings came back within range, there was nothing outside of what we would expect anywhere on the block.
Did the module clamp torque sweep on B03 and there was a run of loose clamps along the east rows which got retorqued, same as the last time on this block, the rest of what I sampled was fine
Drone flight over B01 complete. Two open strings found, ticketed separately. Rest of the block looked normal per the imagery.
Snow clearing on the access roads and the skid pads at B03. Array left to shed on its own per the procedure. Second trip out here this week.
Mowing B08 complete. Two rows skipped, ground too soft.
Went out and did the torque audit on B02, sampled four rack bolts across the block and all of them came back within tolerance so there was no retorquing needed on it at all. Straightforward morning.
MGX33-1744D-0108 PM complete. Filters were loaded, swapped them. Fan bank ok, all six running.
Annual tracker service on TR-B03-R094. Greased the slew drive and checked the backlash which was within spec throughout. Fasteners done as part of it, nothing loose. Row handed back tracking.
CB-B02-02 low current alarm. Water sat in the bottom of the enclosure which I drained out, and the gland has been resealed where it was getting in. One fuse replaced. Currents balanced after.

Rows stowed flat under the snow load per procedure. Released them again once it had cleared two days later. Second trip out here this week, the first time I could not get past the gate for the drift. Nothing damaged.
MV CABLE FAULT between B07 and the collector. Locator put it about 300 ft in. Contractor scheduled.
GF testing on CB-B03-02 and the cans either side of it. Megger readings all came back normal across every string tested. Nothing outside the expected range and nothing to report.

Burned connector on one of the home runs in B03, cut it back and reterminated it, string came back straight away, it was pretty well cooked by the look of it and the insulation had gone brittle around it

XFMR-B03 annual complete. LTC counter checked and recorded, gas relay clear, bushings cleaned down. Second trip out here this week.
Ten broken modules in B01, all replaced from spares. Damage looks like rock strike off the mower deck. Second trip out here this week for this block.
Went ahead and did the ground fault continuity testing on B09, all the readings came back within range, nothing at all to report from it.

kvp36-1641d-0107 wty swap done, took two trips, first part damaged in shipping

Recommend a buried apron is installed along that run rather than continuing to repair it each time.
Burned connector on a home run in B08. Cut back past the damaged section and reterminated it. String current verified after.
b08 clamp check, 8 below spec, retorqued
Feeder relay tripped on B07. Found a failed termination in the switchgear, replaced it.
Soiling station MET-02 cleaned and the reference cell wiped down. The data had looked stuck so I power cycled the logger while I was there and it came back moving.

Walked B03 for soiling and had a good look over the block. Dust accumulation is moderate at the moment, not enough to justify bringing the crew in yet. Will have another look at it next cycle and see where it is then. Nothing else to report from the walk.

Warranty part for CES40-2206A-0333 came in on the truck and I went ahead and installed it with the vendor on the phone walking through the sequence with me. PM sweep on the string inverters in B01. Cleaned the intakes on two units which were both well loaded. One of them has a noisy fan which sounds like a bearing rather than an obstruction, tagged for follow up at the next visit. About 99 out there today.
Did the annual service on TR-Z02, greased the slew drives down the zone and checked the backlash on each of them which was within spec throughout, nothing else to report on it
RTU had locked up overnight. Rebooted it and the points came back. Historian gap only.

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO on CB-B01-18 before opening it up for the annual inspection. Torqued all the lugs as part of it and the IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere in the can. Permit closed at the end of the job.
Torque audit B08. Sampled twelve rack bolts, all within tolerance.

CES40-2404A-0126 failed to start when I got out to it. The cooling fan had failed which I replaced from the site spares we had, and it fired up fine after that and has held since. There was not a great deal else to it, it was a straightforward enough job once I had the cabinet open.

TR-B03-R087 was squealing on the east sweep, same as the others on that block have been doing, the old grease had separated out and gone hard so I cleaned it all out and repacked it properly. These older rows are all coming up to that age together.
TR-B03-R086 stuck at -30 degrees. Motor drawing high current. Replaced the motor, row tracking again.

Pulled the permit and did the GF testing on CB-B06-17 and the cans either side of it, all the megger readings came back normal so there is nothing to report from any of them. Permit closed at the end.

Went out and dealt with the vandalism along the road side, several modules had been shot out again and I documented the lot of them with photos and replaced thirteen from the spares we had. Same stretch as the last time. Report has been filed with the sheriff.
Ground fault continuity testing on B03. All readings came back within range across the block. Nothing to report.
TR-Z08 lubrication and fastener check. Nothing unusual.
Two fuses out in CB-B06-03. Replaced both. Checked the strings for a cause and found nothing. Currents balanced after.
TR-B03-R039 PM; 2 damper bolts loose
PM sweep on the string inverters in B03. Cleaned the intakes on ten units. One had a noisy fan, tagged for follow up.

Coyote had dug under the fence and chewed clean through a home run in B06. Repaired the conductor and patched the fence where it got under. Continuity verified back to the grid ring after the repair. This is now the third incursion along this stretch inside a year and the fabric patch does not hold in that ground. Recommend a buried apron along the run rather than repairing as it happens.
tr-z09 motor rplcd under wty, paperwork uploaded
Row TR-B07-R062 out of alignment with the block. Recalibrated the limits and it is tracking normal now.
KVP36-1847D-0160 tripped on DC GF. Traced it to a pinched connector in CB-B05-08. Replaced the connector and the invertor came back online. It has held since.
KVP36-1837C-0104 DC GF / pinched connector CB-B06-18 / rplcd
Replaced the TR-Z06 motor under warranty. Paperwork and the serial photos have gone up to the claim file. Second one off that zone this year.
spray B06; pre emergent; wind borderline west edge
GF testing on CB-B03-12 and adjacent; megger readings normal; nothing to report

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO at the disconnect before starting. Swapped SLT25-1809A-0922 out for a spare from the shop. Old unit boxed for the RMA. Permit closed at the end of the job and the unit handed back in service.
TR-B07-R060 lubrication and fastener check completed. Nothing unusual found anywhere on the row, all fasteners within spec on the sample.

Warranty part for KVP36-1814B-0349 came in on Tuesday. Installed it with the vendor on the phone walking through the sequence. Unit is back online and holding. Old part is boxed for return, RMA number on the label.

Got called out to an outage on B05 and went out there to it. There was a snake got itself across the bus in the skid which was the end of both it and the outage together. Cleaned all that up and replaced what was damaged in there. The door seal at the bottom of that skid has a gap in it which is presumably how it got in.

Coyote had dug under the fence and chewed clean through one of the home runs in B03, and I went ahead and repaired the conductor and got the fence patched up where it had got under. That is getting to be a regular occurrence along that stretch and somebody ought to put a proper apron in rather than us going out and patching the fabric every few months the way we have been.
Storm walkdown on B03 after the weather came through, there were a few modules with cracked glass which have been tagged up for replacement, everything else looked fine

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO on the affected strings before starting. The warranty replacement modules had arrived earlier in the week so those went into B04, torqued and re-strung per the install sheet. Old modules are on the pallet for the RMA collection. Permit closed and LOTO removed at the end of shift.

Ground fault came up on CES40-2220B-0216 so I went out and walked all the strings on it, there was nothing obvious anywhere and the megger readings all came back fine, so I reset it and it has held since then. Noted the fw rev while I was in the service menu, 4.3.0.
gf testing cb-b03-21 + adjacent, megger normal
Went out and did the cable management repair over in B08, the wire runs had dropped down into the mow path in about seven places, resecured all of them and clipped them back up clear of it
mv fault b01 to collector, locator abt 300 ft in, contractor booked
CB-B01-08 PM. Dust ingress on the lower gland, cleaned it out and resealed. Fuses all good.
Quarterly site walk on B03. Some cable sag on the north rows which will need scheduling before the mow crew comes back through. Rest of the block fine.
mgx33-1743d-0330 pm; sinks cleaned; contactors ok
TR-B05-R051 drive failed at 6 months, well inside warranty. Claim filed, OEM want the old unit back.
CX-R08 HVAC alarm active on arrival. HMI showing compressor short cycling, roughly four minute run then trip. No temperature excursion in the racks yet. Vendor notified, they are coming out Thursday.
GF continuity testing B06. All readings within range.
met-04 cleaned, rsr releveled
storm callout, water in 2 combiner skids B09, isolated and pumped out

Post event walkdown on B08 after last night's weather. Walked every row in the block. No structural damage found anywhere, no glass, no displaced hardware. Checked the drainage at the low end which was running clear. Nothing to report.
Rows stowed flat under the snow load per procedure. Released them again once it had cleared off.
Aerial IR survey B04. Three hot cells flagged, scattered, nothing clustered. Report to the asset manager.
burned connector B03 / cut back / reterminated

Walked B07 for soiling and had a good look over the whole block. The dust accumulation is moderate at the moment, not really enough to justify bringing the wash crew in yet. Will have another look at it next cycle and see where it has got to by then.

Pulled fourteen modules from B08 for the warranty claim. Each one photographed front and back before removal, serial numbers recorded against the claim schedule. Photos and the serial list are in the claim file.

Went out to a string that was out over in B07 and had a look at it, and there was one module in it with the cells shattered up in the corner, the glass still whole but the cells are gone. Swapped it out from the spares we had in the shop and the string came back up to where it should be. There was a hawk sat on the end of the row watching the whole business.

Went out to TR-Z11 on a tracker fault and there was nothing showing at all when I got there, the whole zone was tracking along with the rest of the block and the controller was clear as well. Reset the flag. Nothing else to report on it.

CB-B04-03 and adjacent, megger normal
CES40-1838C-0291 hard fault. Replaced the IGBT module and the invertor came back online, no recurrence through the end of the shift. Nothing else in the log.

GF testing on CB-B02-17 and the adjacent cans. Megger readings all normal, nothing to report.

cb-b04-11 annual, lugs, ir clean

cable mgmt b06, runs had dropped into the mow path, resecured abt 7 spans and clipped them up

perimeter walk, fence ok, washout by south gate filled

Soiling station MET-01 cleaned and the reference cell wiped down. Data had looked stuck so power cycled the logger, came back moving.
Drone flight over B02. Two open strings found, ticketed separately.
High cabinet temp on MGX33-2137C-0339. Filters were completely blocked. Cleaned them out, temp came back down.

TR-B09-R026 was stuck flat at 0 degrees when I got out to it. Had the vendor on the phone for the diagnostics on KVP36-2404A-0196 and we ended up swapping the AC contactor out, it took most of the day between one thing and another, the unit came back up fine after it

Went out and did the PM on KVP36-2415B-0300 and got everything on the sheet done for it. Went ahead and did the tracker PM on TR-Z02, greased all the bearings and checked the damper bolts as part of it, two of them were loose so they got retorqued. There was a hawk sat on the end of the row watching me the whole time.
Mowing on B01 complete. Two rows on the south end were skipped, the ground is still too soft to take the machine down there. Will pick those up on the next pass.

Went out and did the soiling assessment on B08 and the ratio is reading around 6 percent on the reference cells which is up on where it was at the last one. Ground fault on CES40-2041D-0110. Walked the strings, nothing obvious. Meggered ok, reset and it held.
met-04 cleaned, rsr releveled

TR-B05-R003 lubrication and fastener check completed. Nothing unusual found. Row tracking normally.

Went out and did the semiannual on KVP24-1913A-0109 and worked through everything that was on the list for it. mgx33-2024b-0146 dc gf, cb-b07-01, chafed home run against the rack, repaired
TR-Z05 not following. Controller reset did not take. Swapped the tracker motor.

TR-B06-R015 controller was showing offline so I went out and power cycled the TCU at the zone cabinet, and it came back up and tracked normally through the afternoon after that. No obvious reason for it.

Responded to a low current alarm on CB-B04-12. Opening the enclosure found standing water in the base, approximately 25 mm deep. Traced the ingress to a failed lower gland seal. Drained, dried and resealed the gland, torqued the entry. String 16 fuse had failed and was replaced with a 15A. All string currents verified balanced on restoration. This makes three cans on this row with the same gland failure inside twelve months. Recommend the whole row is inspected and resealed as a campaign rather than continuing to respond to individual alarms.
PM on MGX33-2137C-0338. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors checked for pitting, none found. Logged and closed out.
mv fault b04 to collector, locator abt 300 ft in, contractor booked

kvp36-1836c-0255 gf, walked strings, reset held
Walkdown of B04. Nothing significant found in the block. Two modules with cracked glass noted for the punch list.

TR-Z09 was showing a comm fault at the zone controller so I went out and reseated the daisy chain connections and it cleared straight away. Zone tracking normally after that.

Row TR-B01-R093 had come out of alignment with the rest of the block, so I went out and recalibrated the limits on it and it is tracking normal now. CB-B01-03 annual. Lugs torqued, IR scan clean.

Coyote dug under the fence and chewed a home run in B04. Repaired the conductor and patched the fence where it got under.

CES40-2413A-0179 warranty swap is done. It took two trips because the first part turned up damaged in shipping and had to go straight back to them. The second one went in without any trouble and the unit is back in service and reporting normally. Old part boxed with the RMA number on the label.

Post event walkdown on B04 following the weather overnight. Walked all rows. No structural damage found: no bent purlins, no displaced clamps, no glass breakage. Spot checked clamp torque on eight positions in the outer rows, all within spec. Nothing to report from this block.

comms alarm came in overnight, everything was online again by the time i got out there. historian gap only, no production impact. chkd the switch and the media converter, both fine, nothing to do on this one

near miss, loose grating at b08 skid entry, secured and tagged
B07 site walk; cable sag north rows

TR-Z01 annual service. Greased the slew drive and checked backlash, within spec throughout the zone.

Pulled the permit before flying. Drone IR flight over B07 completed this morning. Two open strings were found in the imagery and both have been ticketed separately for somebody to go and look at. The rest of the block looked normal per the imagery. Permit closed at the end of it.
