Washed B05 with the two truck crew and the deionized water. Output up about 5 percent on the next clear day per SCADA. Crew came back after lunch to finish the last two rows.
KVP36-1840D-0402 DC GROUND FAULT. Isolated to CB-B06-08, chafed home run on the rack. Repaired.
More cleanup from the event. TR-B02-R043 two module clamps pulled through. Replaced clamps, no glass damage.
Opened in error.
comms fault slt25-1814b-0996, unit inverting fine, reset the card
10 modules broken B04, rplcd from spares, rock strike

Lightning came through overnight and took out the comms along with one of the surge cards, same as it did over on the far side of the site a couple of summers back. I went ahead and got partial monitoring restored by the middle of the afternoon by moving the critical points onto the card that survived. The rest of it will have to wait until the replacement turns up, and I have ordered two this time so we have a spare on the shelf.
KVP36-1743D-0233 DC ground fault alarm. Isolated to CB-B02-24 where there was a home run chafed against the rack. Repaired and resecured clear. Unit back in service.
outage b01, snake across the bus in the skid, cleaned up, rplcd what was damaged
TR-B05-R051 not tracking, limit switch bracket bent. Reformed the bracket and recalibrated the row. Tracking normally, verified through a full sweep before leaving.

Annual tracker service on TR-Z01. Greased the slew drives down the zone and checked the backlash on each, all within spec. Fasteners done as part of it, nothing loose. Zone handed back tracking normally.

RTU had locked up overnight and I went ahead and rebooted it once I got out there, and all the points came back on their own after that. There is a gap in the historian for the night but no production was lost. The drive out was slow, the county have the road down to one lane past the second turning.
gf on kvp36-1927c-0249. walked the strings, nothing obvious, meggered ok, reset and it held
KVP36-2415B-0281 AC overcurrent trip. Reset, ran fine rest of the day. No pattern.
MOW CREW on site B02, reminded them about the home runs in the rows.

CX-R18 went to standby overnight. Cleared the alarm and it came back in service. Checked the rack voltages and the coolant loop before restoring, both normal. No fault codes stored beyond the standby event itself, so no root cause established for why it went there.
Wash B03 done. Finished ahead of the wind advisory.
Same as the others this month. TR-Z07 repairs. Nine rows needed attention, mostly clamps and dampers. Zone is back tracking with the exception of two rows waiting on parts.
Two fuses out in CB-B08-06, replaced both from the truck. Checked the strings and the terminations for a cause and found nothing at all. Currents balanced after.

Went ahead and did the perimeter inspection and the fence is intact the whole way round with the exception of a washout near the south gate where the drainage cuts under it. Filled that in and packed it down. There was a herd of pronghorn on the far side watching the whole time. Somebody should look at that culvert properly, it is the third time now.
KVP36-1740D-0100 cooling alarm. One fan seized, replaced it, others fine.
TR-Z09 walkdown and repair. Damage concentrated on the west two thirds of the zone. Nine rows touched, mostly clamps and dampers.

Mow crew were on site for B04 and I had the usual word with them about the home runs sitting low in the rows before they got started on it, and they said they would keep an eye out for them the way they always do. The ground was still damp from Tuesday so they were leaving marks on the south side which I mentioned to them as well. They got most of the block done before knocking off.

Had a comms fault come up on SLT25-1732C-0235 so I went out to have a look at it. There is nothing actually wrong with the unit itself as far as I can make out, it was inverting away quite happily the whole time it was showing as offline in the portal. Reset the comms card and it started reporting again after that.

Quarterly site walk on B04. Cable sag noted on the north rows, roughly ten spans hanging lower than they should be. Checked the clips on the affected spans and most have failed at the fixing rather than the cable having pulled through, which points at the clip type. Rest of the block fine. Recommend the rework uses the heavier clip.
kvp36-2413a-0287 pm; filters loaded, swapped; fan bank ok all six

Went out to CB-B03-23 where string 3 was reading zero on the portal, and it was a blown fuse which I replaced and the current came back straight away. Nothing else wrong in the can. The gate code had changed again and nobody told me so I sat there a while first.

Mow crew turned up for B08 and I reminded them again about the home runs sitting low in the rows, same conversation as always, the ground was still damp from Tuesday so they were leaving marks on the south side which I mentioned to them as well, they got most of the block done before knocking off
TR-Z03 out of alignment with the block. Recalibrated the limits, tracking normal.

Did the GF testing on CB-B17-07 and the ones either side of it and all the megger readings came back normal, there was nothing to report from any of them, it was a straightforward morning for once with nothing much to say about it
CB-B06-15 PM. IR clean, currents balanced.
wash crew done b05
Post event walkdown on B06 after last night's weather. Walked the full block, no structural damage found anywhere.
Cable management repair in B02. Wire runs had dropped into the mow path in about eight places, resecured all of them and clipped them back up clear of it.
CX-R12 inspection. Coolant loop and door seals checked, all fine. No alarms on the rack.
Aerial IR survey flown over B03. Eleven hot cells flagged in the report, all scattered with nothing clustered anywhere. Report has gone to the asset manager. Second flight on this block this year.
Pre emergent spray on B06. Wind was borderline so held off on the west edge. Rest of the block treated.
drone ir flight over b08. two open strings found and ticketed separately. rest of the block looked normal on the imagery
CES40-1833C-0172 / vendor diag on the phone / cooling fan swapped / most of the day
Tracker fault TR-B01-R009. No fault when I got there, all tracking. Reset the flag.

Quarterly BESS PM on CX-R14. HVAC filters swapped out and the module voltages checked and balanced, no alarms showing on the rack at any point. It all went smoothly enough and there was nothing that came up needing any further attention on it.
Two fuses out in CB-B03-07 which I replaced. Had a good look for a cause while I was in the can and there was nothing obvious anywhere, no water and no chafing. Currents balanced after.

Went ahead and did the PM on KVP24-2403A-0182 and got everything on the sheet done for it. The heat sinks were cleaned off and the contactors were checked over for pitting, and there was none on any of them. There was a rattlesnake under the skid steps which took some persuading to move on before I could get in there at all. Got it logged and closed out and the unit was reporting fine when I left.
Torque audit B03. Sampled thirteen rack bolts, all within tolerance.
kvp36-2021b-0094, vendor on phone, swapped igbt module, most of the day
PM on KVP24-2135C-0396. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors chkd for pitting, none found. Logged and closed.
Perimeter inspection. Fence intact except a washout near the south gate, filled it.
oil sample xfmr-b05 / dga / bushings ok
TR-Z07 controller was offline so I went out and power cycled the TCU at the zone cabinet. It came back up and tracked normally through the afternoon. idk why these keep dropping.

Lost SCADA on B07. The fiber run tested bad between the skid and B07 so I patched around it on the spare pair and all the points have come back. It needs a permanent repair scheduling, there is no redundancy on that run now.
MOW CREW on site B06, reminded them about the home runs in the rows.

Thirteen modules from B03 have been flagged for the claim, the serials are all recorded and the EL images are attached to the file. They are boxed and staged at the shop ready for collection when the OEM sends someone.
CES40-2039C-0127 AC overcurrent. Reset, ran fine after.

Lost SCADA on B01 overnight and I went ahead and pulled the permit before going into the skid to look at it. The fiber run tested bad between the skid and B01 so I have patched around it on the spare pair for now and the points have all come back. This is not a permanent fix and it needs scheduling properly, which I have said before about this run. Permit closed at the end of it. That is the second fiber run at this site to go the same way and I would suggest somebody looks at how it was installed rather than fixing them one at a time as they fail.

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO on CB-B01-07 before opening it up for the annual inspection. Torqued all the lugs as part of it and the IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere in the can. Permit closed and the LOTO removed at the end of the job.

Went out and did the PM on KVP36-1813A-0121 and got everything on the sheet done for it. Heat sinks cleaned off, contactors checked for pitting and there was none. There was a jackrabbit living under the skid steps that I had to work around. Logged and closed out.
CES40-2040D-0403 PM. Heat sinks cleaned, contacters checked, no pitting.

Pulled the permit for TR-Z06 and did the greasing on the bearings, checked the damper bolts as part of it and two were loose so they got retorqued. Everything else on the checklist was fine. Permit closed at the end of it.
CX-R07 HVAC alarm, the compressor is short cycling, about four minutes then it trips. No temperature excursion in the racks yet. Vendor notified and they are coming out.
TR-Z07 controller offline / power cycled the TCU / came back and tracked normally

Annual on XFMR-B04, checked the LTC counter and the gas relay was clear same as last year, cleaned the bushings down while I was up there, they were dusty but no tracking or weeping that I could see anywhere on them
ces40-2032c-0382 semiannual; filters; vacuum; torque
Combiner PM on CB-B02-11. IR scan showed nothing. String currents balanced per SCADA. Lugs torqued.

PM sweep on the string inverters in B05. Cleaned the intakes on eight units, all were well loaded with dust and one had visible ingress past the filter into the heat sink fins. One unit has a noisy fan, bearing rather than obstruction by the sound of it, tagged for follow up at the next visit rather than dealt with today. The remaining units in the block are due at the next cycle and I would suggest the interval is shortened on this block, they load faster than the ones over on the north side.

Soiling assessment carried out on B02. Soiling ratio reading around 3 percent against the reference cells, which is a little up on the last assessment. Walked the block and the accumulation is light and fairly even across it. Recommending it goes in the next wash cycle rather than being brought forward. Compared the reference cell reading against the walk observation and the two agree.
MET-01 irradiance reading flatlined so I went out to it, the sensor had failed outright and I swapped it for a new one and the readings came straight back where they should be

Pulled the permit before going out to B04 where half the string inverters had shown offline overnight. By the time the permit was done and I was out there they were all back up and reporting normally, which is what happens every time with these. Humidity was high overnight. No production loss at all.
Two fuses out in CB-B01-24, replaced both. Checked the strings for a cause and found nothing at all. Currents balanced after it.
CB-B06-01 string 12 reading zero. Blown fuse, replaced, current came back per SCADA.

Had the vendor on the phone for most of the day walking through the diagnostics on CES40-2411A-0307. It came down to the cooling fan in the end which we swapped out. Took a lot longer than it should have between the hold times and getting the cabinet apart. Unit is back online and running as it should.
walked b03 for soiling. dust accumulation moderate, not washing yet, will look again next cycle
two fuses out cb-b05-18, rplcd both, no cause

TR-Z03 controller was offline when I got the call so I went out and power cycled the TCU at the zone cabinet. It came back up straight away and the zone tracked normally through the rest of the afternoon. No obvious cause for it going down.
cleared volunteer growth along fence b09, several into the fabric
Storm walkdown on B12. A few modules with cracked glass which have been tagged for replacement. Everything else in the block looked fine.
Module wash on B04. Two truck crew with deionized water. Output up about 8 percent on the next clear day per SCADA.
Mow crew on site B03. Reminded them about the home runs sitting low in the rows.
GF continuity testing B04. All readings within range.
CES40-1934C-0206 tripped on DC GF. Traced it to a pinched connector in CB-B04-18. Replaced the connector and the unit came back online. Second trip out here this week.

KVP24-1920B-0357 tripped on AC overcurrent per the HMI at 1447. Reset the unit and it ran fine for the remainder of the day with no further trips off it. No pattern in the fault log going back on this one.
feeder relay tripped on b03. found a failed termination in the switchgear which had let go, rplcd it and got it back in service the same day

Post event walkdown on B01 following last night's weather. Walked every row in the block. No structural damage found: no bent purlins, no displaced clamps, no glass breakage anywhere. Spot checked clamp torque on six positions in the outer rows, all within spec. Nothing to report.

Went out and did the post event walkdown on B08 after the weather came through last night, the road down that side was still greasy so it was slow going, and there was no structural damage anywhere in the block that I could find

KVP36-2432C-0356 tripped on over temperature mid afternoon. Reset at the HMI and it came back and ran the rest of the day without further trouble. Nothing else in the fault log for this unit. Checked the filters and the intake screens while I was there, both clear. Fan bank running, all six. Cabinet temperature had come back to normal by the time I left. No cause identified for the trip.
CX-R20 HVAC alarm. Compressor short cycling. Vendor coming out Thursday.
Two fuses out in CB-B04-13, replaced both. Had a look for a cause and there was nothing obvious anywhere in the can.
KVP36-2421B-0198, vendor on the phone through the diagnostics. Ended up swapping the DC bus capacitor. Took most of the day.
Torque audit on B09. Sampled two rack bolts, both within tolerance. That is a thin sample for a block this size and I would suggest the next audit takes at least a dozen spread across the rows.
Coyote dug under the fence and chewed a home run in B03. Repaired and patched the fence.
mowed B03 / ahead of schedule / extra day

Semiannual PM on KVP36-2343D-0379. Filters replaced, cabinet vacuumed out and the DC bus torque check completed, all connections within spec. Fan bank tested, all six running at full speed. Cabinet temperature at end of PM reading 42 C against an ambient of 34, which is normal for this unit. No faults in the log since the last visit. Nothing to report.

The wind sensor on MET-01 was reading zero when there was obviously wind out there, you could hear it going through the racking. Bearing had gone in the anemometer, same as the one on MET-03 last year. Swapped it out and the readings came straight back. These do not seem to last long in this dust.

Ground fault came up on KVP36-2449D-0196 so I went out and walked all the strings on it, there was nothing obvious anywhere, no chafing and no pinched connectors that I could find, meggered the lot and the readings were fine, so I reset it and it has held since then, sometimes they do that
CB-B01-07 PM / dust in gland / cleaned + resealed
KVP36-2433C-0277 GF / walked strings / nothing found / meggered ok / reset held
MV cable fault between B07 and the collector. Locator put it around 300 ft in. Contractor scheduled. tbd on the date.
Finished the mowing on B06, two rows on the south end had to be left because the ground is too soft to take the machine down there, same as the last cycle, that seep never dries out properly all year
gf testing cb-b04-12 and adjacent, megger readings all normal, nothing to report
Warranty modules installed in B02. Torqued and re-strung, string current back to normal.
kvp36-2421b-0201 down on ac undervolt. poi looked normal on the meters so nothing on that side. reset it and monitored two hours before leaving

Went out and did the PM on KVP24-1932C-0330 and got everything done that was on the sheet for it. The heat sinks were cleaned off and I checked the contactors over for pitting while I was in there and there was none on any of them. It all looked to be in reasonable order. Got it logged and closed out and the unit was reporting normally by the time I left it.
Tracker fault TR-Z09. No fault when I got there, everything tracking. Reset the flag.
kvp24-1906a-0149 fan fault, bird nest in plenum, cleared out
CES40-2211A-0237 PM complete. The filters were loaded so they were swapped out for a fresh set. Fan bank tested and all six are running as they should.
CES40-1831C-0162 in warranty. Case opened with the OEM, waiting on the RMA.
Fourteen broken modules in B06, all replaced from spares. The damage looks like rock strike off the mower deck, same as the last lot. Torqued and re-strung, string current back to normal.

Went out and did the PM on KVP36-2439C-0330 and got everything on the sheet done for it. The heat sinks were cleaned off and the contactors were checked for pitting, there was none on any of them. Logged and closed.
mgx33-2007a-0274 pm, sinks cleaned, contactors ok
aerial ir b05, 4 hot cells, scattered
feeder relay b03, failed termination, rplcd

KVP24-1542D-0324 PM complete. The filters were loaded so they were swapped out for a fresh set. Fan bank tested and all six of them are running as they should be with no noise off any of them. Nothing else came up on the sheet for it.
ces40-2434c-0213 pm, heat sinks cleaned, contactors ok

Got called out to an outage on B03 and went out there to it. There was a snake got itself across the bus in the skid which was the end of both it and the outage. Cleaned all that up, which is not the nicest job going, and replaced what was damaged in there. The door seal at the bottom of that skid has a gap in it which is presumably how it got in and somebody wants to deal with that before it happens again.

Went out and pulled the oil sample off XFMR-B04 and got it shipped away for the DGA, and the bushings all looked alright from where I could see them with no weeping or anything on them. It took a while to find the sample kit, somebody had moved it out of the shop and not put it back. Results should be back in a couple of weeks.

Went out and replaced eight broken modules over in B01 from the spares we had. The damage on all of them looks like rock strike off the mower deck same as the last lot. Torqued and re-strung and the string current came back to where it should be. Not much else to say about it.
CB-B03-12 string 8 reading zero. Blown fuse, replaced it and the current came back. Bloody hot in that skid.
post emergent b08, fence line, records in binder

KVP24-2128C-0179 DC ground fault alarm. Isolated the fault to CB-B05-18 where a home run had chafed through against the rack upright. Repaired the conductor and resecured it clear of the steel. Unit back in service per SCADA.
Post event walkdown on B03 after last night's weather. Walked the full block and no structural damage was found anywhere. Nothing to report.
Pre emergent spray on B02. Wind borderline so held off on the west edge. Rest of the block done.
Finished the mowing on B02, two rows on the south end were left because the ground is still too soft to take the machine down there, same as last cycle, that seep never dries out properly
TR-Z01 not following. Controller reset did not take, swapped the gearbox out. Tracking again.
SLT25-2527C-0612 off network / cycled at disconnect / back up / no prod loss

Mow crew were on site for B05 and I had the usual word with them about the home runs sitting low in the rows before they got started, they said they would keep an eye out for them the way they always do
TR-B02-R003 out of alignment with the block. Recalibrated the limits and verified the row tracked through a full sweep before leaving.
Comms alarm came in but everything was online by the time I got there. Historian gap only, no production impact.

TR-Z01 zone controller showing offline. Power cycled the TCU at the zone cabinet, came back up immediately. Verified the zone tracked through two full moves with all rows in agreement. No fault stored in the controller log, so no root cause established.
comms alarm came in overnight but everything was online by the time i got out there. historian gap only, no production impact. chkd the switch, nothing wrong with it

Torque sweep on the module clamps in B07. Found a run of loose clamps concentrated on the east rows, roughly twenty of them below spec, retorqued all to 18 Nm. Sampled a further thirty across the west rows and those were within tolerance. The east rows are the ones that get the afternoon wind loading so that is consistent. Recommend the next sweep starts on the east side of each block rather than working west to east.
CB-B04-22 string 14 was reading zero. Blown fuse, replaced it and the current came back. Nothing else in the can.
trimmed treeline south of b06, contractor left the brush, chasing them
Ground fault on MGX33-2412A-0379. Walked the strings, nothing obvious anywhere. Meggered ok, reset and it held. No pattern in the log.
MGX33-2018B-0226 semiannual. Filters, vacuum, torque check. No issues.
Trimmed the tree line on the east boundary. It was shading the first two rows through the morning. Cut it back past the fence.

Went out and flew the drone over B01 and got the survey done. Two open strings turned up in the imagery which have been ticketed separately for somebody to go and look at. The rest of the block looked normal enough, nothing else came out of it that was worth chasing up. It was a still morning which made the flying easy for once.
oil sample pulled off xfmr-b07 and sent for dga. bushings look ok from the ground, no weeping anywhere
Quarterly site walk B09. Cable sag on the north rows, will schedule.
Annual tracker service on TR-B02-R029. Greased the slew drive and checked the backlash which came in within spec. Fasteners done as part of it, nothing loose on the row. Handed back tracking.

Burned connector on a home run in B06. Cut back well past the damaged section and reterminated. Verified string current returned to match the adjacent strings. The connector body had discoloured and the insulation was brittle either side, consistent with a poor crimp rather than external damage.
Slew drive on TR-B04-R096 notchy under load. Regreased it, backlash still within spec so leaving it as is.
ces40-1835c-0105 dc gf, pinched connector cb-b05-15, rplcd

High cabinet temp came up on KVP24-1936C-0287 so I went out and had a look at it, and the filters were completely blocked which is what it usually turns out to be. Cleaned them all out and the temperature came back down where it should be within about twenty minutes. Nothing else came up on the unit at all while I was in there. It has been fine since.

Burned connector on one of the home runs in B01, cut it back well past the damage and reterminated it, string current came back up straight away, it was the same style of connector that gave us trouble over in B04 in the spring so worth keeping an eye on
mowing b07 done, two rows skipped, ground soft
ces40-1843d-0345 hard fault; ac contactor rplcd; back online
XFMR-B04 annual complete. LTC counter checked and recorded, gas relay clear, bushings cleaned down. No weeping or tracking noted anywhere on them. Nothing outstanding.
burned connector b07 home run, cut back, reterminated
Quarterly site walk on B02. Some cable sag noted on the north rows. Will schedule the rework.
Drone IR flight over B02. Two open strings found, ticketed separately.
String out in B06. Found a module with the cells shattered, swapped it from spares. Current back.
washed b06, up abt 3% next clear day
Aerial IR survey on B05. Twelve hot cells flagged, all scattered with nothing clustered. Report going to the asset manager.
kvp24-2410a-0359 pm, sinks cleaned, contactors ok
TR-B03-R080 TCU offline / power cycled / back tracking
TR-B04-R061 lube and fastener check. Nothing unusual.

Lightning came through overnight and took out the comms along with one of the surge cards. Got partial monitoring restored by the middle of the afternoon by moving the critical points across onto the card that survived. The rest will have to wait until the replacement turns up.
TR-B02-R068 lube + fastener chk / nothing unusual
tr-b06-r037 not following, reset didnt take, swapped the gearbox
kvp36-2438c-0337 dc gf, pinched connector cb-b06-15, rplcd

TR-B05-R018 was stuck flat at 0 degrees when I got out there. The motor was drawing high current on the meter so I replaced it and the row is tracking again with the rest of the block. Verified it through a full sweep before leaving. tbd whether the old motor is worth sending back.
Torque audit on B05. Sampled nine rack bolts across the block, all came back within tolerance so nothing needed doing on it.
MGX33-2421B-0213 failed to start. Control board had failed, replaced from spares.
Mowing on B05. Growth was ahead of schedule after the rain and it took an extra day to get through the block properly.
CB-B03-12 / water in enclosure / drained + gland resealed / 1 fuse

Went ahead and got the mowing done on B08 and the growth was well ahead of schedule after all the rain, so it took the crew an extra day to get through the block properly. They were off site at the end of the second day.
CB-B03-05 PM / dust in lower gland / cleaned + resealed / fuses ok
CB-B06-23 PM / dust in gland / cleaned + resealed / fuses ok
TR-Z01 warranty gearbox in, OEM watched remotely
Submitted the warranty claim on TR-B01-R048, the drive was inside the coverage window. Paperwork and serial photos have gone up to the claim file. idk how long they take on these.
Regreased the drive on TR-B02-R019. That is the third one in this block this quarter. Normal wear for the vintage on these.

Opened up a warranty case on MGX33-2422B-0362 this morning. The OEM want to see the fault logs before they will authorise anything so I have pulled those and sent them across. Waiting to hear back now. Unit is isolated in the meantime.

Regreased the slew drive on TR-Z08. This is the third drive in this block requiring attention this quarter. Old grease had dried and separated, cleaned out and repacked with fresh. Backlash measured within spec at all positions checked. This block is 2017 vintage and the drives are all coming due at roughly the same time, which is what I would expect for the hours on them rather than anything wrong with the units. Suggest the remainder of the block gets scheduled proactively rather than waiting for each one to start squealing.
Feeder relay tripped on B02. Found a failed termination in the switchgear, replaced it and got it back in service the same day.
washed b02; two truck crew; up abt 8% next clear day

Pre emergent application on B01. Started at the north end at 0700 with wind at approximately 4 mph. Wind picked up after lunch to a sustained 12 to 14 mph with gusts higher, which is over the label limit for this product, so stopped at that point. Approximately 60 percent of the block was treated. Remaining area is the south third and will be completed tomorrow morning if conditions hold. Buffer at the drainage was maintained throughout.
5 modules broken b02, rplcd
PM sweep on the string inverters in B01. Cleaned the intakes on two units which were both well loaded. One had a noisy fan, tagged for follow up at the next visit.

KVP36-1646D-0137 hard faulted and would not restart. Fault log pointed at the DC bus. Opened the cabinet and found the DC bus capacitor bank had failed, one can visibly bulged. Replaced the capacitor from site spares. Verified DC bus voltage at 1042 V on restart, within the expected band. Unit has run through to end of shift with no recurrence. Ruled out a gate driver issue, those tested fine. This unit is a 2016 build and this is the first fault I have seen on it.
Mowed B07. Growth was ahead of schedule after the rain and it took an extra day to get through the block properly. Crew signed out at the end of the second day.
MET-01 pyranometers cleaned, rain gauge done, RSR releveled.

Had a near miss reported to me this morning, a contractor crew had gone into B16 without checking in with anybody and without the LOTO on the skid being verified. Stood the whole crew down for the rest of the morning and rebriefed them all on the check in procedure before letting them back to work on it.
Pre emergent spray on B02. Wind was borderline so held off on the west edge. Rest of the block treated.
CES40-2010A-0190 DC GF. Isolated to CB-B06-05, chafed home run against the rack. Repaired.
Mowed B01, and the growth was ahead of schedule again after all the rain, so it took an extra day to get through it. Crew were reminded about the home runs before they started.

Went out and replaced six broken modules over in B04 from the spares, and the damage on all of them looks like rock strike off the mower deck, same as we have had before on that block. I have had a word with the crew about it again. The drive down was fine, they have graded the road since I was last out. Torqued and re-strung and the string current came back to where it should be.
TR-B04-R070 was stuck out at -30 degrees. The motor was drawing high current on the meter so I replaced it and the row is tracking again with the rest of the block. About 97 out there.
Walkdown of B08 completed and there was nothing significant to report from the block at all, it all looked to be in reasonable order. Two modules with cracked glass which have gone on the punch list.
Feeder relay tripped on B03. Found a failed termination in the switchgear which had let go. Replaced it and got it back in service the same day.

POI breaker tripped at approximately 0210 taking the whole plant off line. On site by 0300. Relay targets indicated a fault external to the plant. Contacted the utility control room who confirmed the event was on their side, a fault on the transmission line feeding the interconnect. Walked the collector, the MV switchgear and the main transformer while awaiting their clearance, found nothing on our equipment. Restored under their coordination at approximately 0815, so roughly six hours off line. No damage and nothing to action on the plant side. Meter readings recorded for the availability calculation.
String out in B07. Found a module with the cell area shattered, swapped it from spares and the string came back up to where it should be.
CES40-2430C-0176 hard fault. Replaced the cooling fan and the invertor came back online, no recurrence through the end of the shift. Nothing else showing in the log for it.
Storm walkdown B06. Few cracked glass, tagged. Rest fine.
KVP36-2044D-0253 no start. DC contacter failed, rplcd from spares.
Replaced the drive on TR-B02-R053, the old grease had hardened right up and the gear faces were scored, same as the others on that block, row is back in service now
CB-B05-18 string 13 reading zero. Blown fuse, replaced it and the current came back.

PM on CB-B03-15 today, and there was dust getting in through the lower gland the same way as the one I did over in B02 last month, so cleaned it all out and resealed it, the fuses were all good and the currents looked balanced, road in was rough after the grader went through
cable mgmt b06, 3 spans resecured

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO before opening CB-B04-20 for the annual inspection. Torqued all the lugs as part of it and the IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere in the can. Permit closed out and the LOTO removed at the end of the job.

Went out and did the pre emergent on B04, the wind was borderline through the morning so I held off on the west edge and did the rest of it, same as I had to do on B02 a couple of weeks back, the records are in the binder

Went out and did the annual inspection on CB-B14-11 and torqued the lugs while I had it open, and the IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere in it. Nothing much else to report from this one.
CB-B05-21 string 14 reading zero. Blown fuse, replaced and the current came back.

Ground fault came up on CES40-2006A-0310 so I went out and walked all the strings on it looking for a cause, and there was nothing obvious anywhere at all, no chafing and no pinched connectors that I could find. Meggered the lot and the readings came back fine, so I reset it and it has held since then.

CES40-2341D-0099 hard faulted, and it was the DC bus capacitor which had gone, one of the cans was swollen up, replaced it from the site spares and it came back up fine, 3.9.7 was loaded while I was in there and it took about twenty minutes and came back clean
brush clearing b05, heavier than last cycle

Went ahead and power cycled the TCU on TR-Z09 which had shown offline, and it came back up straight away and tracked normally through the rest of the afternoon. There was no obvious reason for it dropping out in the first place that I could find. There were a pair of hawks working the rows the whole time I was out there.
string out in b06, found a module with the cells shattered up in the corner, glass still whole but the cells are gone. swapped it from spares and the string came back up
Combiner PM on CB-B04-16. IR scan showed nothing. String currents balanced per SCADA. Lugs torqued.

Went out to TR-Z09 on a tracker fault that had come in and by the time I was standing in front of it there was nothing wrong at all, the whole zone was tracking as it should and there was nothing showing at the controller either. Reset the flag and left it. These come and go and I could not tell you what causes it.
Module wash on B08. Two truck crew with the DI water. Output up about 8 percent on the next clear day per SCADA.
Quarterly torque check on module clamps in B06. Three found below spec and retorqued to 18 Nm. The rest sampled OK across the block.

Pulled the permit and briefed the mow crew before they got started on B07, and had the usual word with them about the home runs sitting low in the rows. They said they would keep an eye out for them, same as always. Permit closed at the end of the day when they signed out.
ir scan b02, 11 warm cells scattered, nothing clustered, no action
TR-B08-R090 controller reset, back online. Verified the row tracked through a full sweep afterward.
Pulled five modules from B05 for the warranty claim. Boxed and staged for pickup, photos and serials recorded in the file.
CES40-1844D-0187 PM. Heat sinks cleaned, contacters checked for pitting, none found. Closed.
cleared the volunteer growth along the fence at b02, several of them had grown right into the fabric and had to be cut out properly rather than just trimmed
PM on MGX33-2415B-0280. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors checked for pitting, none found. Logged and closed.

KVP24-1935C-0219 PM complete, the filters were loaded so they were swapped out for a fresh set, and the fan bank was tested with all six of them running as they should be with no noise off any of them

Cleaned the pyranometers and the rain gauge on MET-02 and releveled the RSR while I was up there, same as always, the bubble had drifted a fair way off which it does at this one, it is a windy spot and the mast moves more than it should
MGX33-2416B-0221 AC overcurrent. Reset, ran fine after. No pattern.
CES40-2419B-0129 PM complete. Filters were loaded, swapped them. Fan bank tested ok, all six running.
Ground fault on MGX33-1729C-0356. Walked the strings, nothing obvious. Meggered ok, reset and it held.
Walked B07 for soiling and had a good look over the block, the dust accumulation is moderate at the moment and not really enough to bring the crew in for yet, will have another look next cycle
kvp36-2432c-0356 down ac undervolt, poi ok, reset, monitored 2hr
Quarterly site walk on B08. Cable sag noted on the north rows which will need scheduling before the mow crew comes through. Rest of the block looked in reasonable order.

Feeder relay tripped on B04 overnight and I got out there mid morning, and there was a failed termination in the switchgear which had let go properly and made a mess of the cubicle. Replaced the termination and got the whole thing cleaned up and back in service by the afternoon. Photos of the old one are in the file.
Cabinet temperature alarm on KVP36-2432C-0361. Reading high but under the trip point per the HMI. Nothing obviously wrong inside. Left it running.
POI breaker tripped and took the whole plant down. Utility said it was on their side of the interconnect. Restored after coordination with them, about three hours off. Nothing on our equipment.

MV cable fault between B05 and the collector. The locator put it at about 300 ft in from the block end and I shot it a second time from the collector side which agreed. Both ends isolated and grounded and tagged out. Contractor is scheduled.
TR-B08-R019 drive failed at 5 months, well inside warranty. Claim filed, OEM wants the old unit back.
Went out and did the post event walkdown on B05 after the weather last night, and there was no structural damage anywhere in the block that I could find at all, everything looked as it should

Did the PM on CES40-2341D-0095 and got everything on the sheet done, the filters were loaded so they were swapped out for a new set, and the fan bank was tested with all six running as they should be. Checked the rev while I was in the menus, 5.1.0, nothing pending from the OEM on it. Same as the last one I did on that row.

TR-B05-R038 controller showing offline. Power cycled the TCU at the zone cabinet and it came back up immediately. Verified the row tracked through two full moves in agreement with the block. No fault stored in the controller log so no root cause established.

Burned connector on a home run in B01. Cut back well past the damaged section and reterminated. Verified string current returned to match the adjacent strings. The connector body had discoloured and the insulation was brittle either side, consistent with a poor crimp rather than external damage.

CES40-2214B-0109 would not start at all so I went out to it, ended up being the gate driver which had failed, swapped one in from the site spares and it fired up fine after that, it is running 5.1.0 which I noted down, flagged it for the next update window in case there is anything newer

Went out on a tracker fault for TR-B02-R071 that had come in overnight. The drive over was slow, there was a crew working on the county road. When I got to the row there was no fault at all, everything was tracking along with the rest of the block and the zone controller was clear. Reset the flag and watched it for a bit. Nothing else worth noting.

Went out to SLT25-2036C-0672 which was not reporting and I went ahead and reseated the comms module and the RS485 leads while I had it open, and it has been fine since then. These do this from time to time and there is usually not a great deal to it at all. It was a wet morning and the track down there was greasy.
9 modules broken B05, rplcd from spares, rock strike
Post emergent on B07, spot treated the fence line. Records in the binder.

Lightning event overnight took out the site comms along with one surge card on the RTU rack. Restored partial monitoring by mid afternoon by moving the critical points onto the surviving card. Approximately 40 percent of points remain dark until the replacement arrives. No production impact, the plant ran through the whole event. Two replacement cards ordered so we hold a spare.
mgx33-1801a-0215 ac overcurrent trip, reset, ran fine rest of the day, no pattern in the log
KVP24-1913A-0113 down on AC undervoltage. POI looked normal on the meters. Reset and monitored for two hours, no further trips. tbd if it recurs.
Mow crew on site for B04. Reminded them about the home runs sitting low in the rows. They know.

Had the vendor on the phone walking me through the diagnostics on KVP24-2139C-0106 and it took most of the day between the hold times and getting the cabinet apart. Ended up being the control board which we swapped out and it came back up fine.
brush clearing b01; heavier than last cycle; wet spring

CES40-2412A-0347 is still inside the parts warranty so opened a case with the OEM rather than touching it. Fault logs pulled and attached to the case. Waiting on the RMA number before anything gets removed from the unit. Unit remains isolated and tagged in the meantime, block is running on the remaining units. Will follow up if nothing comes back inside a week.
KVP36-2432C-0357 tripped on over temperature mid afternoon. Reset at the HMI, came back and ran the rest of the day. Nothing else in the fault log.
Went ahead and did the herbicide on B05 per the plan and the buffer was maintained at the drainage the whole way along. Records are written up in the binder. Nothing else to report from it.
kvp36-2423b-0265 hard fault; gate driver rplcd; back online; no recurrence

Had the vendor on the phone walking through the diagnostics on CES40-1836C-0233 and it took the best part of the day between the hold times and getting the cabinet apart. It ended up being the DC contactor which we swapped out and the unit came back up fine afterwards. The LOTO was in place the whole time and the permit was closed out at the end of the shift.
b01 clamp check, 3 below spec, retorqued

Comms alarm came in but everything was already online by the time I got out there. Historian gap only, no production impact from it. Checked the switch and the fiber patch, both fine. Ambient was 107 by mid afternoon.

Semiannual PM on KVP36-2430C-0303. Filters replaced, cabinet vacuumed out and the DC bus torque check completed, all connections within spec. Fan bank tested, all six running at full speed with no bearing noise. Cabinet temperature at end of PM reading 44 C against an ambient of 36, normal for this unit. No faults in the log since the last visit.

Responded to a low current alarm on CB-B02-17. On opening the enclosure there was standing water in the base, approximately 20 mm. Traced the ingress to a failed lower gland seal. Drained, dried and resealed the gland, torqued the entry. String 9 fuse had failed and was replaced with a 15A. Verified all string currents balanced on restoration. This is the second can on this row with the same gland failure in six months and I would suggest the rest of the row is inspected rather than waiting for alarms.

Pulled the permit before going out to TR-Z02 on a tracker fault that had come in overnight. By the time the permit was sorted and I was out at the zone there was no fault showing at all and everything was tracking along with the rest of the block. Reset the flag and had a look at the controller which was clear as well. Permit closed at the end of it.
Drone IR flight over B03. Two open strings found and ticketed separately. Rest of the block normal.

Module wash on B09 with the two truck crew and the deionized water. Output up about 5 percent on the next clear day per SCADA, which is about what this block returns. Walked two rows behind the crew afterward to check the coverage and the glass is clean with no streaking on the lower edges. Water pressure and nozzle spacing were as specified. Crew signed out mid afternoon.
Cabinet temperature alarm on KVP36-2426B-0290. Reading high but under the trip point per the HMI. Nothing obviously wrong inside. Left it running.
Row TR-B05-R046 had come out of alignment with the rest of the block. Recalibrated the limits and it is tracking normal now. Watched it through a couple of moves.
Went out to do the post event walkdown on B05 after the weather last night, drive in was fine, no structural damage anywhere in the block that I could find. Nothing to report on this one.

Feeder relay tripped on B02 overnight and I got out there mid morning, there was a failed termination in the switchgear which had let go properly and made a mess in the cubicle, replaced it and got the whole thing cleaned up and back in service by the afternoon, photos of the old one are in the file
Site tripped overnight. Relay targets pointed at the main feeder. Walked the collector and found nothing visible anywhere. Restored under supervision mid morning.
mowing b06 done, 2 rows skipped, ground soft
cable mgmt b08, 12 spans dropped into the mow path, resecured
tr-z07 pm, bearings greased, 2 damper bolts loose

KVP36-1635C-0371 cooling alarm on the HMI. Opened the cabinet and found one of the six fans seized, bearing had gone. Replaced it from spares. Remaining five tested and all running at full speed. Cabinet temperature came back into normal range within the hour. Filters were clean, changed at the last PM. No other faults in the log for this unit.
met-02 wind sensor zero, bearing gone, swapped

TR-B07-R011 was not following the rest of them so I went out to it, tried a controller reset first and that did not take at all, ended up swapping the gearbox out same as the one I did over on R046 a while back, row is moving again now

Quarterly site walk on B02. Cable sag noted on the north rows, roughly a dozen spans hanging low enough that they will be at risk when the mow crew comes through. Checked the clips on the affected spans and several have failed rather than the cable having pulled loose, which suggests the clip type rather than installation. Rest of the block is fine. Recommend the rework uses the heavier clip we went to on B05.
ces40-2431c-0210 ac undervolt, poi ok, reset, monitored
kvp36-1802a-0379 hard fault; cooling fan rplcd; back online; no recurrence
Burned connector on a home run in B07. Cut back and reterminated. Verified string current after.
kvp36-2408a-0124 down on ac undervolt. poi looked normal on the meters so nothing on that side. reset it and monitored two hours before leaving, no further trips
SLT25-1825B-0433 offline in portal / generating fine per meter / comms fw a couple revs back / flagged for next window

Feeder relay tripped on B08 during the night and I got out there mid morning. There was a failed termination in the switchgear which had let go and made a mess of the cubicle. Replaced it and cleaned up, back in service by the afternoon.
Swapped SLT25-2005A-0976 out for a spare from the shop. Old unit is boxed and labelled for the RMA. Unit came online and is reporting normally per the portal. Nothing else in that string.
B04 clamp check / 3 below spec / retorqued to 18 Nm
Comms alarm came in but everything was online by the time I got there. Historian gap only, no production impact.
B02 storm walk / few cracked glass / tagged / rest ok

CES40-2414B-0337 threw a DC ground fault alarm so I went out and isolated it down to CB-B04-24 where there was a home run chafed clean through against the rack upright, the insulation was worn right down to the conductor on it. Repaired the run and got it resecured properly clear of the steel with a standoff rather than just a tie the way it was. Unit is back in service and the fault has not come back. That is the second one like it on that block and I would say it is worth somebody walking the rest of the runs there.

Went out to KVP24-1603A-0093 which had thrown a cooling alarm, and one of the fans had seized on it so that was replaced and the others all tested fine. It came back up without any trouble after that and has been running as it should since. Nothing else came up while I was in there.

CB-B03-01 string 10 was reading zero on the portal. Blown fuse, replaced it and the current came straight back up. Had a look for a cause while I was in there and found nothing obvious at all. Bloody hot in that skid.
cb-b01-10 low current alarm. water in the bottom of the enclosure, drained it, resealed the gland and rplcd one fuse
Wash B04 done. Finished ahead of the wind advisory.
ces40-2409a-0196 semiannual, filters, vacuum, torque check
KVP36-2435C-0234 tripped on over temperature mid afternoon. Reset at the HMI, came back and ran the rest of the day. Nothing else in the fault log. Checked the filters and the intakes, both clear.
kvp36-2437c-0384 fan fault / bird nest in plenum / cleared
Post event walkdown B04 after last night's weather. No structural damage found.

TR-Z12 was stuck out at -45 degrees when I got to it. Motor drawing high current on test, consistent with a failed winding. Replaced the motor and the row is tracking again, verified through two full moves. Checked the drive and the backlash while I was on the row, both within spec, so the motor is the only issue here. This is the second motor failure on this zone inside eighteen months and it is worth pulling the run hours on it.
RTU locked up overnight, the historian shows a gap from about 0200. Rebooted it and all the points came back. No production impact.

Grass fire along the south fence, the fire department handled it and had it out before I got there. Checked the array over afterward and there is no damage to any of the modules, the fence fabric is scorched in one place but sound.
Scheduled wash on B04 completed, and the crew got finished ahead of the wind advisory that came in that afternoon. Coverage looked alright on the rows I walked behind them.
Replaced the TR-B02-R002 motor under warranty. Paperwork and serial photos uploaded.

Did the ground fault continuity testing on B03 and all the readings came back within range, nothing outside what we would expect anywhere on the block, it took most of the morning to work through it all
Tracker fault on TR-B02-R016. No fault when I got there, everything tracking. Reset the flag.

Went out and dealt with a burned connector on one of the home runs in B04, cut it back well past the damage and reterminated it and the string came straight back up, the insulation had gone brittle for a good way either side of it

Lightning came through overnight and took out the comms along with a surge card, same as it did over on the other side of the site two years ago, got partial monitoring back by the middle of the afternoon so at least we can see most of the plant, the rest is going to have to wait until the replacement card turns up, and I have ordered two this time
feeder relay b07, failed termination, rplcd

Went ahead and got the mowing done on B03, and the growth was well ahead of schedule after all the rain we have had so it took an extra day to get through it properly. There was a badger set up at the far end that the crew had to work around.
KVP36-2430C-0306 failed to start. Found the IGBT module had failed, replaced it from site spares.
Replaced the TR-Z06 motor under warranty. Paperwork and serial photos uploaded to the claim.
Combiner PM CB-B05-06. IR scan showed nothing. Currents balanced per SCADA.
kvp24-1601a-0333 dc gf, pinched connector cb-b01-07, rplcd

ground fault came up on kvp24-1610a-0147 so i went out and walked all the strings on it, nothing obvious anywhere, no chafing and no pinched connectors that i could find. meggered the lot and the readings were fine so i reset it and it has held since
KVP36-2436C-0275 was derating all afternoon, output down maybe 10% against its neighbours. No fault logged, nothing to reset. Watched it recover after sundown.
MGX33-1740D-0301 DC ground fault. Isolated to CB-B08-17, chafed home run against the rack. Repaired and back in service.
Finished the mowing on B02, two rows had to be left because the ground is still too soft down there to take the machine, they will get picked up on the next pass once it has firmed up a bit
Twelve broken modules in B04, replaced from spares. Damage looks like rock strike off the mower deck. Mow crew notified.
Replaced two fans in the KVP36-2421B-0205 fan bank, the bearings were noisy on both. Others tested ok. Cleaned the plenum out while I was in there.
KVP36-2413A-0291 PM complete. The filters were loaded so they were swapped out for a new set. Fan bank tested, all six running as they should be. Nothing else on it.

Scheduled wash on B03 completed. The crew got finished ahead of the wind advisory that came in later on. I walked a couple of rows behind them to check the coverage over and it looked alright, no streaking anywhere.
wrong site closing
Outage on B02. Found a snake across the bus in the skid, which was the end of it and the outage both. Cleaned up and replaced what was damaged in there.
CES40-1836C-0234 / vendor diag / control board swapped / all day
CES40-2001A-0208, vendor on the phone for the diagnostics. DC bus capacitor swapped. Took most of the day.
B05 walkdown. Nothing significant. Two cracked glass for the punch list.
Two fuses out in CB-B08-14. Replaced both. Checked for a cause, nothing found.
Reworked the sagging home runs in B07 before the mow crew gets there.

SCADA showed KVP36-2421B-0196 offline so I drove out expecting a comms issue, but the invertor was in fault and had stopped itself. Restarted it and it came back online and ran the rest of the day. Nothing else in the log.
Aerial IR survey on B05. Five hot cells flagged, all scattered, nothing clustered. Report going to the asset manager. idk if they want us to action any of them at this level.
Pulled seven modules from B05 for the warranty claim. Boxed and staged for pickup. Photos and serials in the file.
Opened in error.

KVP36-2419B-0361 keeps derating in the afternoon heat. Got the OEM support line on the phone, they had me pull logs and send them in. Case opened, no answer yet. Third time on a Kelvara unit this summer with the same story. Might be a fan control thing rather than the fans themselves. Nothing I can prove.

Grid fault ride through event took MGX33-2413A-0264 offline at about 1420 per the HMI. It had cleared on its own and resynced before I arrived on site. Verified the output was normal against the neighbouring units. Second one of these this month at this site.
feeder relay B03 / failed termination in switchgear / rplcd

Went out and dealt with a burned connector on a home run in B02, cut it back past the damage and reterminated it, the string came straight back up. Drive out was fine, the road has been graded since last time.

TR-Z03 showing a comm fault at the zone controller. Reseated the daisy chain connections and it cleared straight away. Zone tracking normally after that. That is the second time on this zone in about two months.

Coyote had dug under the fence on the west side and chewed through a home run in B05. Repaired the conductor and patched the fence where it got under. Recommend the fence line gets walked on the next PM cycle.
Module clamp torque sweep on B04. Found a run of loose clamps concentrated on the east rows, all retorqued to spec. Rest of the sample was fine.
SCADA showed KVP36-2430C-0305 offline. Drove out expecting a comms issue but the unit was in fault and had stopped itself. Restarted, back online.
MV cable fault between B09 and the collector. The locator put it at about 300 ft in from the block end. Both ends isolated and tagged out, contractor is scheduled.

CX-R03 module fault. Isolated the affected string and called it in to the OEM. Rack voltage on the isolated string reading approximately 40 V below its neighbours, which is consistent with a module level failure rather than a BMS fault. Remainder of the rack is in service and cycling normally. OEM have the fault codes and are reviewing. Left isolated pending their response.
TR-B07-R053 TCU offline. Power cycled, came back, tracking.
tr-b02-r080 not following; reset didnt take; swapped limit switch
KVP36-2419B-0373. Fan bank all running but the airflow across the stack felt low to me. Pulled the filters and cleaned them, they were not that dirty. Temperture came down some after.

Perimeter inspection completed. Fence intact the full run with the exception of the washout near the south gate where the drainage cuts under it. Filled and packed it down. Checked the fabric either side of the washout and it is sound. This culvert is undersized for the volume it takes and this is now the fourth time it has cut through. Recommend it is addressed properly rather than filled again.
cb-b07-20 low current, water in the enclosure, drained and gland resealed, one fuse
kvp24-1923b-0153 high cab temp, filters blocked solid, cleaned, temp came back down
storm walk b03, few cracked glass tagged, rest ok

Washed B06 with the two truck crew and the deionized water. Output up about 4 percent on the next clear day per SCADA.

Went out and did the post emergent on B05, spot treating along the fence line where the growth comes through worst, and the drive down was slow because the county have the road tore up past the second turning. KVP24-1917B-0310 tripped DC GF. Traced to a pinched connector in CB-B06-05. Replaced, back online.
fence and gate check, camera 3 lens fogged, wiped it

b03 washed, only under 2% back this cycle, down on what it used to do

kvp36-2426b-0289 derating all afternoon, down maybe 12% on its neighbours, no fault logged

Went out and did the torque audit over on B02, sampled ten rack bolts across the block and every one of them came back within tolerance so nothing needed doing. It all went smoothly enough and there is not a lot else to report from it.
scada showed kvp36-2432c-0354 offline, drove out expecting comms, unit was in fault and had stopped itself. restarted, back online

Replaced the drive on TR-B05-R096, the old grease had hardened right up and the gear faces were scored where it had been running dry, same as the others on that block have been going, row is back in service and tracking properly now, that is the fourth one this quarter and they are all the same vintage so it is not a surprise
