Module wash on B01. Two truck crew with deionized water. Output up about 8 percent on the next clear day per SCADA.
Two fuses out in CB-B01-08. Replaced both. Checked the strings for a cause, nothing found. Currents balanced after.
Module wash on B05 with the two truck crew and the deionized water. Output up about 4 percent on the next clear day per SCADA. Crew off site mid afternoon.
TR-B07-R052 controller offline. Power cycled the TCU, came back tracking.
wrong site closing
mgx33-2430c-0138 dc gf, pinched connector cb-b02-10, rplcd
TR-B05-R037 out of alignment, limits recalibrated

Got called out to an outage on B02 and went out to it, there was a snake got itself across the bus in the skid which was the end of both of them, cleaned all that up and replaced what was damaged in there, not the nicest job going and that is the second one this year
Washing crew completed B07. Ag dust was heavy on the lower rows before they started.
flew b02 for ir, 11 warm spots, under the limit, closing out
Combiner PM on CB-B05-02. IR scan showed nothing in the can. String currents balanced per SCADA. Lugs torqued.
tr-z01 not following. controller reset didnt take so swapped the gearbox out. tracking again now
TR-Z01 annual service. Greased the slew drive and checked the backlash which was within spec. Came back after lunch to finish the far end of the zone.
Mowing on B03. Growth was well ahead of schedule after the rain so it took an extra day to get through the block properly. Crew signed out at the end of the second day.
PM on MGX33-2024B-0146. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors checked for pitting, none found. Logged and closed.
7 modules broken B07, replaced from spares, rock strike off the mower

Somebody had a go at the fence over at B01 overnight and taken off with some of the grounding conductor, not a huge amount but enough. I went ahead and filed the report with the sheriff and got the fence patched up the same day, and we have replaced the conductor that was taken. There is a camera covering that corner but it was pointed the wrong way.
ces27-1548d-0778 iso fault, damp am, cleared when it dried
tr-b06-r021 tracker pm, bearings greased, damper bolts chkd, two were loose so retorqued them. rest of the row fine
CES40-2435C-0302, vendor on the phone through the diagnostics. DC contactor swapped out. Took most of the day.
Mowing on B06. Growth was well ahead of schedule after the rain and the crew needed an extra day to get through the block properly. Crew signed out at the end of it. tbd on shortening the interval.
POI tripped, plant down. Utility side. 6 hrs off.
KVP36-2420B-0355 down on AC undervoltage. POI looked normal on the meters. Reset and monitored for two hours, no further trips.

Went out and did the storm walkdown on B07 after the weather came through. Had a good look round the whole block. There were a few modules with cracked glass which have been tagged up for replacement, and other than that everything else looked to be in reasonable shape. Nothing structural that I could see anywhere. Will leave the tagged ones for the next replacement round unless somebody wants them done sooner.

TR-B01-R009 was stuck out at -45 degrees when I got to it. The motor was drawing high current which is usually the sign, so it was replaced and the row is tracking again now. Nothing else that I noticed on the row while I was there.
cb-b08-13 low current, water in the enclosure, drained and gland resealed
Torque audit on B07. Sampled eight rack bolts, all within tolerance. No retorquing needed.

Burned connector on a home run in B01. Cut back well past the damaged section and reterminated. Verified string current returned to match the adjacent strings. The connector body had discoloured and the insulation was brittle either side, consistent with a poor crimp rather than external damage.

Tree line trimming along the east boundary. The growth was shading the first two rows through the morning and showing in the string data for those rows. Cut back well past the fence line so we should get more than one season out of it this time. Brush piled at the north gate for the chipper. Recommend the trim interval on this boundary is annual rather than every other year, the growth rate here does not suit the current schedule.
TR-B03-R053 greased and fasteners checked. Nothing found out of order.
IR on B02. 11 warm cells, more than last flight but still scattered and under threshold. No ticket.

Lost SCADA on B04. The fiber run tested bad between the skid and B04 so I patched around it on the spare pair and the points came back. Second trip out here this week. It needs a permanent repair scheduling.
Near miss reported. Loose grating at the B03 skid entry, someone nearly went through it. Secured it and tagged for repair.

Got called out after the storm came through and there was water in two of the combiner skids over in B04. Went ahead and isolated both of them and got them pumped out. The road down to that side of the site was under water in two places so it took a while to get there at all, had to go round through the neighbour's gate in the end. Both skids are dried out and back in service now and I have put in for the gland seals to be looked at on that whole row because this is not the first time.
Replaced two fans in the KVP36-2423B-0268 fan bank, the bearings were noisy on both of them. Others tested ok. Cleaned the plenum out while I was in there. Temperture came down after.
CB-B02-01 PM. Dust ingress on the lower gland, cleaned it out and resealed. Fuses all good.

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO before opening it up. CES40-1833C-0172 would not start at all. Found the DC bus capacitor had failed, one of the cans was visibly swollen. Replaced it from site spares and the unit came back up fine. Permit closed and the LOTO removed at the end of it.

Went out to CES40-2146D-0396 which had flagged a fan fault and had a look at it. There was a bird nest built up in the intake plenum, a fair sized one, which I cleared out of there. The fans were running fine once it was clear and the cabinet temperature came back down where it should be. Nothing else came up on the unit.
String out in B06. Module with shattered cells, swapped it from spares. Current back.

Went and did the cable management repair over in B10, the wire runs had dropped down into the mow path in about fourteen places which is the worst I have seen it on that block. Resecured all of them and put extra clips in where the fixings had failed rather than the cable pulling through.
Tracker fault TR-Z11. No fault when I got there, everything tracking. Reset the flag. tbd.
KVP36-1927C-0249 cooling alarm. One fan seized, replaced it from spares. Others tested and running fine.
tr-z09 stuck at -30, motor high current, rplcd
mowed b05, ahead of schedule, extra day
two fuses out cb-b04-19, rplcd both, no cause found
Same units in B06 dropping out again. Logged it. No action, they come back on their own.
TR-B01-R077 damper bolt loose. Retorqued to spec and verified the row through a full sweep.
MET-01 cleaned, RSR releveled
CES40-2415B-0355 tripped on DC GF. Traced it to a pinched connector in CB-B02-03 which I replaced, and the invertor came back online after that. It has held since.

Lost SCADA on B02 overnight, same as B05 did back in the spring, the fiber run tested bad between the skid and the block so I patched around it on the spare pair and got the points back, it needs a proper repair scheduling and that is the second run at this site now
Finished the mowing on B04, two rows were skipped because the ground was too soft to take the machine, they will get picked up on the next pass once it firms up a bit
ces40-1823b-0354 pm, sinks cleaned, contactors ok, rev 5.2.1
B02 clamp check. 5 below spec, retorqued to 18 Nm. Rest sampled OK.
POI tripped, plant down. Utility side. 6 hrs off.
Tracker fault TR-B06-R092. No fault when I got there, all tracking. Reset the flag.

Went out and did the ground fault continuity testing on B01 and everything came back within range, there was nothing that stood out on any of the strings I tested. Took most of the morning to work through the block. Nothing to report on this one.
kvp24-1642d-0107 no start, igbt failed, rplcd from spares
Storm walkdown B06. Few modules with cracked glass, tagged them. Rest looked fine.
TR-Z12 warranty repair. The OEM shipped the wrong revision first time round so that had to go straight back to them, the second one fit fine and went in without any trouble. Zone tracking again.
CX-R12 HVAC alarm, compressor short cycling. Vendor coming out.
KVP36-2419B-0371. Fan bank all running but airflow across the stack felt low. Pulled and cleaned the filters, they were not that dirty. Temps came down some.
oil sample xfmr-b08 shipped for dga; bushings ok
washed b01, up close to 5% next clear day

Went ahead and got the mowing done on B02 and the growth was well ahead of schedule after all the rain we have had, so the crew needed an extra day to get through the block properly. Same as last cycle really, that block always runs ahead of the rest because of the drainage down the middle of it. They were off site at the end of the second day.
CB-B06-11 low current / water in enclosure / drained + gland resealed / 1 fuse
kvp36-2418b-0271 second overtemp this season, reset again, intake and sinks clear
cb-b01-22 str 3 zero, fuse, rplcd

Went up for the walkdown on B04 and had a good look round the block, there was nothing significant to report from it, everything looked to be in reasonable order. Two modules with cracked glass which have gone on the punch list for the next replacement round.

Did the tracker PM on TR-B04-R090, greased the bearings and went over the damper bolts, two of them were loose so they got retorqued, the rest of it was fine, there was a fair bit of standing water at the end of the row from the storm on Tuesday
kvp24-1612a-0350, vendor on the phone walking me thru the diagnostics. ended up swapping the cooling fan. took most of the day between the hold times and getting the cabinet apart

Pulled the oil sample off XFMR-B03 and got it shipped for DGA, took a while because the sample kit was not where it should have been, bushings all look alright from the ground, no weeping that I could see on any of them.
Quarterly site walk on B09. Cable sag noted on the north rows. Will schedule the rework.
washed b02, two truck crew, di water. output up abt 8% next clear day per scada
Quarterly torque check on the module clamps in B06. Five came back below spec and were retorqued to 18 Nm. Rest sampled OK.

Went out with the wash crew for B02, the two truck setup with the deionized water same as usual, and they got through the whole block in the day which was better going than I expected. Output came back up about 8 percent on the next clear day per SCADA which is a good result for that one. There were jackrabbits under the rows making a nuisance of themselves but no harm done to anything. Crew were off site by five.
MGX33-1742D-0354 flagged a fan fault. Found a bird nest in the intake plenum, cleared it out. Fans fine after that.

Washed B04 again with the two truck crew and the deionized water, same as last time, and the output came back up about 2 percent on the next clear day per SCADA which is about what we usually see out of that block, crew was in and out by mid afternoon, no problems

RTU had locked up overnight and I went out and rebooted it once I got there, and all the points came back on their own after that. There is a gap in the historian for the night but nothing was lost in terms of production at all as far as I can see.
10 modules broken B10, rplcd from spares, rock strike
CB-B10-22 PM / dust in gland / cleaned + resealed / fuses ok
KVP24-2348D-0403 cooling alarm. One fan seized, swapped it. Others fine.
Combiner PM on CB-B06-21. IR scan showed nothing of note. String currents balanced per SCADA. Lugs torqued. tbd whether the next round needs the full block or just a sample.
Lost SCADA on B05. Fiber run tested bad between the skid and the block, patched around it on the spare pair. Permanent fix needs scheduling.
Opened in error.

Quarterly site walk on B05. Cable sag noted on the north rows, roughly ten spans hanging lower than they should be, will schedule the rework before the mow crew comes through. Rest of the block looked to be in reasonable order.
KVP36-2436C-0278 failed to start. IGBT module had failed, replaced from spares.
Module wash on B10. Two truck crew with the deionized water. Output up about 8 percent on the next clear day per SCADA, which is a good result for that block.

Did the PM on MGX33-1702A-0257 today, cleaned the heat sinks off and checked the contactors for pitting which there was none of, same as the last time I did this one, got it logged and closed out before lunch
MET-03 irradiance reading flatlined. Sensor had failed, swapped it out and the readings came straight back.
Feeder relay tripped B04. Failed termination in the switchgear, replaced it.
Mowed B04. Growth was well ahead of schedule after all the rain and it took an extra day to get through the block properly. Crew signed out at the end of the second day.
cb-b04-15 annual, lugs torqued, ir clean
two fans rplcd kvp36-2418b-0271, bearings noisy
Mowing on B07 complete. Two rows skipped, ground was too soft to take the machine.
oil sample pulled off xfmr-b07 and shipped for dga. bushings look ok from the ground, no weeping or tracking anywhere on them
GF testing on CB-B04-03 and adjacent. Megger readings normal, nothing to report.
Mowing on B02 complete. Two rows skipped, ground too soft to take the machine.
TR-Z07 tracker fault. No fault present when I got there, everything TRACKING with the block. Reset the flag and watched it through a move.
String out in B05. Found a module with the cell area shattered, glass still whole. Swapped it from spares, string current back to normal.
Second overtemp on KVP36-2419B-0371 this season. Reset it again. Checked the intake and the heat sinks, both clear. Noted fw 4.2.1 on this one, not sure if that is current.

Torque audit on B02. Sampled eleven rack bolts spread across four different rows rather than concentrated in one, all came back within tolerance. No retorquing required. Nothing else noted on the walk.
same units B01 dropping out again, no action
String out in B07. Module with shattered cells, swapped it from spares.

The wind sensor on MET-02 was reading zero when there was obviously wind out there. Bearing had gone in the anemometer. Swapped it out for a new one and the readings came straight back. This is the third anemometer at this site in two years and the dust is the likely reason.
aerial ir b05, 5 hot cells, scattered, report to AM

Went out to CB-B07-24 on the low current alarm and there was water sat in the bottom of the enclosure which I drained out, and the gland has been resealed where it was getting in. One of the fuses had gone and that was replaced. Currents were back to normal when I left it.

Row TR-B06-R092 had come out of alignment with the rest of the block, same as one further along did back in the spring, so I recalibrated the limits on it and it is tracking normal now, watched it through a couple of moves before I left to make sure it stayed put, these seem to drift on this block more than the others
Sprayed B08. Had to stop early, the wind picked up after lunch and got over the label limit. Rest tomorrow.
wash crew done b03, under 2% back, less than last round, panels looked clean

Feeder relay tripped on B08 during the night and I got out there about nine, found a failed termination in the switchgear which had let go properly, made a mess in the cubicle, replaced the termination and cleaned it all up and got it back in service by early afternoon, photos of the old one are in the file
mgx33-1742d-0354 ac overcurrent, reset, ran fine after. fw 3.9.7, matches the block

Quarterly site walk on B04. There is cable sag on the north rows which will want scheduling before the mow crew comes back through. Came back after lunch to finish the far end of the block. Rest of it looked reasonable enough.
GF testing on CB-B07-13 and the adjacent cans. Megger readings all normal, nothing outside the expected range on any string. Nothing to report.

Did the ground fault continuity testing on B04 and all the readings came back within range, nothing outside of what we would expect anywhere on the block, it took most of the morning to work through it
kvp36-2428c-0165 fan bank all running but airflow felt low across the stack. pulled and cleaned the filters, not that dirty. temps came down some

CES40-1821B-0362 threw a DC ground fault alarm so I went out and isolated it down to CB-B03-06 where there was a home run chafed clean through against the rack upright. Repaired the run and got it resecured properly clear of the steel. The unit is back in service and the fault has not come back since. Firmware on this one is 5.0.4 which matches the rest of the block.
GF testing on CB-B07-01 and the adjacent cans. Megger readings all normal per the meter. Nothing to report.
XFMR-B07 annual. LTC counter checked, gas relay clear, bushings cleaned. Nothing wrong with it.

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO on CB-B07-21 before opening it up for the PM. The IR scan showed nothing at all in the can and the string currents were balanced per SCADA. Lugs torqued as part of it. Permit closed and the LOTO removed at the end of the job.
Opened a warranty case on KVP36-1847D-0164. OEM want the fault logs before they authorise anything. Sent them over.
cb-b01-08 str 6 zero, fuse blown, rplcd

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO on the string before starting, walked it with the site lead. Warranty replacement modules had arrived earlier in the week so installed those in B05, torqued to spec, re-strung and verified. Old modules are on the pallet for the RMA collection. Permit closed out and LOTO removed at end of shift.

Site tripped overnight and I got out there first thing, the relay targets were pointing at the main feeder so I walked the whole collector run looking for something and there was nothing visible anywhere at all, no damage and nothing burned. Restored it under supervision mid morning and it has held since then.

High cabinet temp came up on KVP36-2440D-0389 so I went out to it, the filters were completely blocked which is what it usually is, cleaned them out and the temperature came back down where it should be
Swapped two fans in KVP36-2432C-0357, bearings noisy. Others ok. Cleaned plenum.
cable mgmt B07 / 10 spans
TR-Z12 drive replaced; grease hardened; gear faces scored; row back in service
Quarterly site walk on B01. Cable sag noted on the north rows, will schedule the rework before the mow crew comes through.

Went out and pulled the oil sample off XFMR-B03 and got it away for the DGA, and the bushings all looked to be in reasonable order from the ground with no weeping or tracking on any of them that I could see. There is nothing else to report on this one, the results should be back in a couple of weeks and somebody can have a look at them then.

Post emergent application on B09, spot treated along the fence line. Wind steady at around 6 mph, within label limits throughout. Approximately 55 litres of mix used. Buffer maintained at the drainage. Containers triple rinsed and disposed per procedure, records written up in the binder before leaving site.
Warranty modules installed B02. Torqued and re-strung, current back to normal.
Mow crew on site for B01 and I reminded them again about the home runs sitting low in the rows before they started on it, same conversation as every cycle with that lot
cb-b05-15 string 9 reading zero on the portal. blown fuse, rplcd it and the current came straight back. nothing else wrong in the can
Ground fault on KVP24-2128C-0185. Walked the strings, nothing obvious. Meggered ok, reset and it held.

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO before starting. KVP36-2409A-0126 had tripped on DC GF. Traced the fault down to a pinched connector in CB-B03-13 which was replaced. Unit came back online and has held since. Permit closed out and the LOTO removed at the end of the shift.
Went ahead and did the ground fault continuity testing on B08 and all the readings came back within range with nothing outside of what we would expect anywhere on the block at all
KVP24-2137C-0338 down on AC UNDERVOLTAGE. POI looked normal on the meters so nothing wrong on that side. Reset the invertor and monitored it for two hours before leaving. No further trips.
Cable management repair in B10. Wire runs had dropped into the mow path. Resecured about three spans and clipped them up clear.
RTU locked up overnight. Rebooted and the points came back. Historian gap only.

Copper theft attempt at B01. Fence cut on the road side and a quantity of grounding conductor taken, approximately 30 m by my estimate from what is missing. Report filed with the sheriff, incident number in the file. Fence patched the same day and the conductor replaced and reconnected. Continuity verified back to the grid ring after the repair. The camera covering that corner does not reach the point where they cut through and I would recommend it is repositioned.
TR-Z01 out of alignment, limits recalibrated

Opened a warranty case with the OEM on CES40-2443D-0325 following the fault last week. They will not authorise anything until they have the full fault logs, so pulled those off the unit and uploaded them to the case this afternoon. Unit remains isolated and locked out in the meantime. Expect a response inside five working days per their terms. Case number is in the file.

Responded to a low current alarm on CB-B08-18. On opening the enclosure there was standing water in the bottom, roughly 15 mm deep. Traced the ingress to a failed seal on the lower cable gland. Drained the enclosure, dried it out, resealed the gland and torqued the entry. String 12 fuse had failed, presumably from the moisture, replaced with a 15A. Currents on all twenty four strings verified balanced after restoration. Recommend the adjacent cans on this row are inspected for the same gland failure, they are the same vintage and the same installer.
TR-B01-R083 was stuck out at 60 degrees when I got to it. Motor drawing high current on the meter so I replaced it. Row tracking again with the rest of the block.
Comms alarm, everything was online when I arrived. Historian gap only, no production impact.

Two fuses out in CB-B03-02 which I replaced from the truck, and I had a good look for a cause while I was in there and there was nothing obvious at all, no water and no chafing anywhere. Currents balanced after it.

Burned connector on one of the home runs in B05, cut it back well past the damaged section and reterminated it, string came back up straight away, it had got hot enough that the insulation was brittle for a good six inches either side of it

Went ahead and power cycled the TCU on TR-B03-R012 which had shown offline, and it came straight back up and tracked normally through the rest of the afternoon. No obvious reason for it dropping out that I could find.

Went out and reworked the sagging home runs over in B06 before the mow crew gets down there, there were a fair number of spans hanging low enough to get caught up and they have all been clipped back out of the way now
Vandalism, several modules shot out along the road side. Documented the lot with photos and replaced fourteen of them from spares. Report filed.
CB-B01-04 string 6 reading zero on the portal. Blown fuse, replaced it and the current came straight back. Checked the strings either side while I was in there and both are reading normally.
Fence and gate check completed. The lens on camera 3 was fogged so I wiped it down. Rest of the perimeter is sound with no breaches.
Walkdown of B04 completed. Nothing significant found. Two modules with cracked glass noted and added to the punch list.
TR-B02-R057 tracker PM; bearings greased; damper bolts chkd, two loose so retorqued

Storm walkdown on B03 after the weather came through. There were a few modules with cracked glass which I have tagged up for replacement in the next round. Everything else in the block looked fine to me.

Did the annual inspection on CB-B08-04, torqued all the lugs while I had it open and the IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere in the can, it was hot enough in that skid that I was glad to get the doors shut and get out of it
Reworked the sagging home runs in B07 before mowing gets there. All clipped back up clear.
RTU locked up overnight. Rebooted, points came back.
TR-Z13 tracker fault. No fault when I got there, everything tracking with the block. Reset the flag.

Two fuses out in CB-B06-12, both replaced. Checked the affected strings and the terminations either side for a cause and found nothing: no chafing, no water ingress, connectors all sound. Currents verified balanced on restoration. No explanation for the failures, worth noting if this can comes up again.
KVP36-2428C-0169 keeps derating in the afternoon heat. Got the OEM support line on the phone, they had me pull logs and send them in. Case opened, no answer yet.

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO on the row before starting the job. The drive on TR-B02-R070 was replaced, the old grease had hardened right up and the gear faces were scored where it had been running dry. New drive went in without any trouble and the row is back in service and tracking with the block. Permit closed and signed off at the end of the shift.
Quarterly torque check on the module clamps in B02. Three found below spec and retorqued to 18 Nm. The rest of what I sampled across the block was all within tolerance per the wrench.
CB-B05-04 low current alarm. Water in the bottom of the enclosure, drained it and resealed the gland. One fuse replaced.
CB-B03-06 string 2 reading zero. Blown fuse, replaced it and the current came straight back.

Copper theft attempt at B02. Fence cut on the road side and a quantity of grounding conductor taken. Report filed with the sheriff, incident number in the file. Fence patched the same day and the conductor replaced and reconnected, continuity verified back to the grid ring after.
Walkdown of B09. Nothing significant. Two cracked modules noted for the punch list.
kvp24-1643d-0303 pm, sinks cleaned, contactors ok
cb-b06-22 string 8 reading zero on the portal. blown fuse, rplcd it and the current came back straight away. nothing else in the can that i could see
mowed b03, ahead of schedule, extra day

Burned connector on one of the home runs in B01, cut it back well past the damage and reterminated it, string came straight back up afterwards, the connector body was discoloured and the insulation had gone brittle either side of it
Ground fault on CES40-2427C-0337. Walked the strings, nothing obvious anywhere. Meggered ok, reset and it held. No pattern in the log.

KVP36-2434C-0084 fan bank all running but the airflow across the stack felt low to me. Pulled the filters and cleaned them, they were not that dirty at all which is what makes me wonder. Temperature came down some after. Checked the intake screens and the plenum, both clear. All six fans turning at what looks like full speed. Nothing I can point at as the cause.
fence and gate check. camera 3 lens fogged, wiped it
Scheduled wash on B07 completed. Crew finished ahead of the wind advisory that came through that afternoon. Coverage looked good on the rows I walked.

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO on CB-B03-04 before opening it up for the PM. The IR scan showed nothing at all in the can and the string currents were balanced per SCADA. Lugs torqued as part of it. Permit closed and LOTO removed at the end of the job.

KVP36-1738C-0137 PM complete. Filters were loaded so they were swapped out. Fan bank tested, all six running fine. 2.8.3 was installed while I was in there, took about twenty minutes and it came back clean.
drone over b04, two open strings ticketed
Feeder relay tripped on B03 and I got out there mid morning, there was a failed termination in the switchgear which had let go, replaced it and got it back in service the same afternoon

KVP24-2205A-0375 PM complete. Filters were loaded and have been swapped for a fresh set. Fan bank tested, all six running at full speed with no bearing noise. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors inspected and no pitting found. Cabinet temperature normal at end of PM. Nothing outstanding on this unit.

Feeder relay tripped on B02 in the night, and I got out there mid morning after the gate business got sorted out, there was a failed termination in the switchgear which had let go properly and made a mess in the cubicle, replaced it and got the whole thing cleaned up and back in service by the afternoon

Went out to SLT25-1741D-0209 which had dropped off the network again, and it is the same story every time with these ones, by the time I got out there it had already come back on its own after a power cycle at the AC disconnect. The production was never affected at any point, the meter has it inverting away the whole way through, it is purely the reporting that drops out and then comes back on its own. Logged it and left it alone, there is nothing to be done about it that I can see.
TR-B08-R092 was out of alignment with the rest of the block. Recalibrated the limits and it is tracking normally now.
CES40-1833C-0174 / vendor diag on the phone / DC contactor swapped / most of the day
same units B07 dropping out again / no action / self recover
Outage on B06. Found a snake across the bus in the skid, which was the end of both it and the outage. Cleaned up and replaced what was damaged in there.
Mowing on B14 complete. Two rows skipped, ground was too soft to take the machine safely.
storm callout, water in 2 combiner skids B01, isolated, pumped out

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO on the string before starting work. Burned connector on one of the home runs in B04. Cut it back well past the damaged section and reterminated it. Verified the string current came back afterward. Permit closed at the end of the job.

MV cable fault between B06 and the collector, and the locator put it at about 300 ft in from the block end which I shot a second time from the collector side and got the same answer. Both ends have been isolated and grounded and tagged out for now. The contractor is scheduled to come out and excavate and splice it.
mow crew b09, reminded them re the home runs
oil sample xfmr-b08 sent for dga, bushings ok, no weeping

Cleaned the soiling station on MET-03 and wiped the reference cell down, the data had looked stuck for a couple of days so I power cycled the logger while I was there and it started moving again after that
PM sweep on the string inverters in B06. Cleaned the intakes on eight units, they were well loaded. One had a noisy fan, tagged for follow up.
KVP36-2413A-0295 tripped on AC overcurrent per the HMI. Reset the unit and it ran fine for the remainder of the day. No pattern in the fault log for it.

CES40-2009A-0151 threw a DC ground fault alarm. Isolated it to CB-B04-15 where I found a home run chafed against the rack upright. Repaired and resecured clear of the steel. Came back after lunch to verify, unit is running normally.

Smoke reported at the B09 skid. No fire on arrival. Heavy discoloration on one MV termination, the compound had run and there is tracking visible on the surface of the elbow. Isolated the feeder, grounded and locked out. Insulation resistance on the affected phase reads low, the other two are normal, which is consistent with a partial discharge failure developing rather than a flashover that has already happened. Left isolated and tagged pending engineering. Recommend the remaining terminations in this skid are tested before anything is re energised, they were all made off by the same crew at the same time.

Comms alarm raised overnight. On arrival every point was already online and reporting normally. Historian shows a gap of approximately four hours with no production impact, the meter reading over the period is consistent with the irradiance. Checked the switch, the media converter and the fiber patch, all normal. No fault found and no root cause established, which is the third comms alarm at this site in two months with no explanation.

MGX33-2018B-0226, vendor on the phone through the diagnostics. IGBT module swapped. All day job.

Ground fault on KVP36-2423B-0268. Walked the strings, nothing obvious. Meggered ok, reset and it held.
Mow crew on site for B07. Reminded them about the home runs sitting low in the rows.

Finished the mowing on B08 and two rows on the south end were skipped because the ground is still too soft to take the machine down there. Came back after lunch to walk behind them and there is no damage to the cabling.
CB-B01-23 PM; IR clean; currents balanced

lost scada b06, fiber bad, patched around it

CB-B17-15 PM. Found dust ingress on the lower gland, cleaned it out and resealed. Fuses all good and currents balanced.

Meter readings recorded for the availability calculation.
TR-Z01 was not following the rest of the block. Controller reset did not take so the tracker motor was replaced. Zone tracking again after that.
mgx33-2022b-0245 ac overcurrent, reset, ran fine after

Site tripped overnight. Relay targets pointed at the main feeder. Walked the collector and found nothing visible anywhere. Restored under supervision. idk what caused it, nothing in the logs.

Feeder relay tripped on B02. Found a failed termination in the switchgear, the compound had run and the connection let go. Replaced the termination and cleaned out the cubicle. Insulation resistance verified normal on all three phases before restoration. Back in service by early afternoon.
TR-Z03 squealing, grease separated, cleaned and repacked

Stowed the rows flat under the snow load per the procedure, and it was a job getting out there at all, the access road had drifted over past the second gate and I had to wait for the plow. Released them again once it had cleared off two days later. Nothing damaged as far as I can tell.
mow crew b07, reminded them re home runs

Went out to do the post event walkdown on B16 after the weather last night, the road down the west side was still under water in places so I came round the long way, and the block itself had no structural damage anywhere that I could find, everything looked as it should

burned connector b04; cut back; reterminated
ces40-2424b-0211 semiannual, filters, vacuum, torque
storm walkdown b01, a few cracked glass, tagged them, rest looked fine

TR-B02-R058 out of alignment with the block. Recalibrated the limits and verified through a sweep.
CES40-2414B-0327 PM complete. The filters were loaded so they were swapped out for a fresh set, and the fan bank was tested with all six running as they should be.
String out in B04. Found a module with the cell area shattered, glass still whole but the cells are gone. Swapped it from spares. Second trip out here this week for this block.
Half the string inverters in B03 showed offline overnight, all back by the time I arrived. Humidity was high. No production loss.

TR-Z02 warranty repair. The OEM shipped the wrong revision first time round so that had to go straight back, the second one fit fine and went in without trouble. Zone tracking again and the paperwork has gone up to the claim.

Oil sample pulled from XFMR-B02 and shipped for DGA. Bushings inspected visually from ground level, no weeping, no tracking and no compound migration on any of them. Gas relay checked and clear. Results expected inside two weeks. Nothing to report pending those.
two fuses out cb-b01-18, rplcd both, no cause
String out in B06. Module with a shattered cell area. Swapped it.

Mow crew were back on site for B04 and I had the usual conversation with them about the home runs sitting low in the rows before they started. They said they would keep an eye out for it. We will see how that goes, it is the same crew as last time.
TR-Z01 stuck at 60 degrees. MOTOR drawing high current, replaced it. Tracking again.
Annual tracker service on TR-B02-R051. Greased the slew drive and checked the backlash which was within spec. Fasteners done as part of it.
mgx33-1714b-0183 ride thru, self cleared, output ok
CES40-2425B-0208 DC ground fault alarm. Isolated to CB-B05-19, found a chafed home run against the rack. Repaired and returned to service.

Ground fault came up on KVP36-2138C-0313 so I went out and walked all the strings on it looking for a cause. Nothing obvious anywhere, no chafing and no pinched connectors. Meggered them and the readings came back fine. Reset it and it has held.
mgx33-1740d-0301 high cab temp, filters blocked, cleaned, temp came down. fw rev 5.0.4 noted
rtu locked overnight, rebooted, points back
TR-Z08 drive replaced. The old grease had hardened and the gear faces were scored. Row back in service. idk how many more of these are due.
tr-z07 lube and fastener chk, nothing unusual

Cleaned the pyranometers and the rain gauge on MET-03. Both domes had a film on them, worse than the last visit. Releveled the RSR, the bubble had drifted noticeably. Compared readings against MET-01 afterward and the two now agree closely.

Went up for the walkdown on B08, and the drive out was slow with the mud after all the rain we have had this week. Nothing significant in the block itself, it all looked reasonable. Two modules with cracked glass which I have noted on the punch list for the next replacement round. Gate was locked behind me on the way out.
Replaced the TR-Z05 motor under warranty. Paperwork and serial photos have gone up to the claim file. Second trip, the first part was the wrong revision.

SLT25-2118B-0761 had gone offline so I went out and reset it at the disconnect and it came back up without any trouble. There was nothing obviously wrong with it that I could see while I was there. It has been reporting fine since.
tr-z13 lube chk, nothing unusual
Walked B06 for soiling. Dust accumulation is moderate at the moment, not enough to bring the crew in yet. Will look again next cycle.
10 modules from B08 flagged for the claim. Serials recorded, EL images attached.

Went up for the quarterly site walk on B04, gate code had changed again and nobody had told me so I sat there a while. There is cable sag on the north rows which will need scheduling before the mow crew comes back through. Other than that the block looked alright. The fence on the west side wants looking at too.
Warranty modules installed B01 / torqued + re-strung / string current normal

Went out and did the soiling assessment on B01 and the ratio is reading around 6 percent on the reference cells which is well up on where it was at the last one. I went ahead and walked the block as well and the accumulation is heavier on the lower third of the modules the way it usually goes. Recommending this block is brought forward into the next wash cycle rather than waiting for the scheduled one to come round.
Drone flight over B02. Two open strings, ticketed separately.
Torque audit on B03. Sampled eight rack bolts across the block and all of them came back within tolerance so there was no retorquing needed. Nothing else noted on the walk round.

Row TR-Z03 had come out of alignment with the rest of the block so I went out and recalibrated the limits on it and it is tracking normal now. The drive out was slow, they had a truck jackknifed on the county road. Watched it through a couple of moves before I left.

Fourteen broken modules in B06, all replaced from spares. The damage looks like rock strike off the mower deck, same as the last lot we did on this block. Torqued and re-strung and the string currents came back to normal against the adjacent strings. Mow crew have been told again.
Coyote had dug under the fence and chewed through a home run in B05. Repaired the conductor and patched the fence where it got under. That is the second one this year along that stretch.
mgx33-1722b-0211 down AC undervolt, poi normal, reset

Went and reworked the sagging home runs in B05 ahead of the mow crew getting there, there were a good number of spans down low enough to catch, all clipped back up now, the ground is still soft down that end after the rain

TR-Z04 showing a comm fault at the zone controller per the HMI. Reseated the daisy chain and it cleared.

TR-B02-R046 was not following the rest of the block so I went out to have a look at it. Tried a controller reset first which did not take, so ended up swapping out the gearbox on it. Row is moving again now. There was a bit of back and forth getting the right part number off the shelf but we got there in the end.
Walkdown of B01. Nothing significant. Two cracked modules for the punch list.
Wash B09 done. Crew finished ahead of the wind advisory.

Went ahead and recalibrated the limits on TR-Z07 which had come out of alignment with the rest of the block, it is tracking normal now and I watched it through a couple of moves before I left. There was a bobcat sat up on the end of the row watching the whole thing.

TR-Z02 was not following the rest of them. Controller reset did not take so swapped the gearbox out. Zone tracking again after that. idk why these keep going on this site.

Perimeter inspection completed. Fence intact for the full run with the exception of a washout near the south gate where the drainage cuts under. Filled it and packed it down. Checked the fabric either side of the washout and it is sound. The culvert there is undersized for the volume it gets and this is the third time it has cut through in two years. Recommend it gets looked at properly rather than filled again.

Went out to a string that was out over in B01 and had a look at it, and there was one module in it with the cells shattered up in the corner, the glass still whole but the cells gone. Swapped it out from spares and the string came back up.
torque audit b03, 11 bolts, all in tolerance
mgx33-1740d-0301 no start; ac contactor failed; rplcd

Nothing to action, left in service.

TR-Z03 was not following the rest of the block so I went out to it. Tried a controller reset first which did not take at all, so ended up swapping the gearbox out on it. Zone is tracking again now. There was a fair bit of back and forth finding the right part number on the shelf.

TR-Z05 tracker PM. Bearings greased, damper bolts checked, two were loose and retorqued.

Reworked the sagging home runs in B02 ahead of the mow cycle. About ten spans had dropped low enough to be at risk. Resecured and clipped clear. Several clips had failed at the fixing rather than the cable pulling through.
Warranty part for CES40-2112A-0221 came in, installed it with the vendor on the phone. Old part going back on the RMA.

Did the PM on KVP36-2440D-0393 and got through the whole sheet on it, the filters were fairly loaded so they were swapped out for a new set, and the fan bank was tested with all six of them running as they should be. Same as the last one I did on this row really. Nothing came up.

cb-b07-07 pm, dust ingress on the lower gland, cleaned it out and resealed. fuses all good, currents balanced
CX-R04 HVAC alarm. Compressor short cycling. Vendor coming out.
mgx33-2430c-0138, vendor diag, swapped cooling fan, 5.1.0 loaded, clean

Went out to TR-Z05 on a tracker fault that had come in overnight. By the time I was out there everything was tracking along with the rest of the block and there was no fault showing at the zone controller either. Reset the flag and left it. Nothing else to report.

walked b04 for soiling, dust moderate, not washing yet

KVP24-1915B-0398 down on AC undervoltage. POI looked normal. Reset and monitored two hours.
B03 soiling ratio abt 5% on ref cells, recommending wash next cycle
CB-B02-03 PM / IR clean / currents balanced

kvp36-2409a-0103 semiannual, filters, vacuum, torque, ok

rtu locked up overnight, rebooted it, points all came back, historian gap only
torque audit b01, 4 bolts ok

b03 clamp check, 3 below spec
CES40-1830C-0296 PM. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors checked, none pitted.
Post event walkdown on B08 after the weather last night. No structural damage found anywhere in the block. Nothing to report.

Went out and did the post emergent on B07, spot treating along the fence line where the growth comes through worst, and got the records written up into the binder afterwards. Nothing much else to say about it, the conditions were about right for it and it went as planned.
TR-B07-R042 out of alignment with the block. Recalibrated the limits and verified through a full sweep.
CB-B03-20 and adjacent, GF testing. Megger readings normal. Nothing to report.
TR-B03-R080 tracker PM. Bearings greased, damper bolts checked, two loose and retorqued.

Went out and did the semiannual on MGX33-1647D-0263 and got everything on the sheet done. The filters were replaced and the cabinet vacuumed out, and the torque check was done on the DC bus. Nothing came up on it.

cb-b04-07 pm, ir scan clean, currents balanced per scada
ces40-2442d-0377 pm, sinks cleaned, contactors ok, closed

cb-b05-15 annual, lugs torqued, ir clean

MV cable fault between B08 and the collector. Locator put it about 300 ft in. Contractor scheduled.

Same units in B02 dropping out again, same as last time and the time before that, logged it and left it alone because they come back on their own every time without anybody doing anything to them, there is no production lost by any of it as far as the meter is concerned, it is just the reporting that goes
kvp24-1912a-0220 gf, walked strings, reset held

Site tripped overnight. Relay targets pointed at the main feeder. Walked the full collector run, the switchgear and both riser structures in daylight and found nothing visible: no tracking, no burning, no damage to any termination. Insulation resistance spot checked on two feeders, both normal. Restored under supervision mid morning and it has held since. No root cause established, which I am not happy about. Recommend the relay event record is pulled and reviewed by protection engineering rather than leaving this as an unexplained trip.

Module clamp torque sweep on B04. Found a run of clamps below specification concentrated on the east rows, eighteen in total, all retorqued to 18 Nm. Sampled a further forty across the remaining rows, all within tolerance. The east rows take the afternoon wind loading at this site which is consistent with the pattern seen on the previous sweeps. No module or glass damage associated with any of the loose clamps.

Ground fault came up on KVP36-1845D-0156 so I went out and walked all the strings on it looking for a cause, and there was nothing obvious anywhere at all, no chafing and no pinched connectors that I could find on any of them. Meggered the lot and the readings all came back fine, so I reset it and it has held since then.
Drone IR flight over B05. Two open strings found, ticketed separately.
GF testing on CB-B08-11 and the adjacent cans. Megger readings all normal across every string tested. Nothing to report.
Post event walkdown on B07 after last night's weather. Walked the full block and no structural damage was found anywhere. Nothing to report.

Went out and flew the drone over B08 for the IR survey and got the whole block done in the one flight. Two open strings turned up in the imagery which have been ticketed separately for somebody to go and have a look at, and the rest of the block came back looking normal enough. Still morning, good conditions for it.
TR-B07-R030 PM; greased; 2 bolts

Next sweep due in the autumn cycle.
KVP24-1626B-0257 tripped on DC GF. Traced it to a pinched connector in CB-B06-17. Replaced the connector and the unit came back online.

KVP36-2427C-0381 PM complete. Filters were loaded and were replaced with a fresh set. Fan bank tested, all six running at full speed with no bearing noise on any of them. XFMR-B08 annual complete. LTC counter checked and recorded, gas relay clear, bushings cleaned down. Nothing noted, no weeping or tracking.

Quarterly torque check on the module clamps in B02, five of them came back below spec and were retorqued to 18 Nm, the rest of what I sampled was all within tolerance so nothing else needed doing on it
TR-Z11 drive failed at 14 months, well inside warranty. Claim filed, OEM wants the old unit back.
Semiannual on CES40-2043D-0175. Filters rplcd, cabinet vacuumed, DC bus torque chkd. No faults.
cb-b05-11 pm, dust in gland, cleaned and resealed

Quarterly site walk on B05. Cable sag noted on the north rows which will want scheduling before the mow crew comes back through. Rest of the block fine.

Went out and did the perimeter inspection and the fence is intact the whole way round with the exception of the washout near the south gate where the drainage cuts under it. Went ahead and did the annual inspection on CB-B06-12, torqued all the lugs while I had it open and the IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere. It was 103 in that skid by lunchtime so I was glad to get out of it.
aerial ir b07, 12 hot cells, scattered, nothing clustered, report to AM
cb-b02-12 pm, dust in gland, cleaned and resealed

Drone IR flight over B03. Two open strings found and ticketed separately.

KVP24-2343D-0129 PM complete. Filters loaded, swapped them. Fan bank ok.
TR-B07-R060 tracker PM. Bearings greased, damper bolts checked, two loose so retorqued.

tr-z07 not following, swapped limit switch

tr-z10 tracker pm. bearings greased, damper bolts chkd, two loose so retorqued

SLT25-2142D-0837 is showing offline in the portal but it is generating away normally per the meter. The firmware on the comms board is a couple of revs back so I have flagged it for the next update window. tbd.
KVP24-1607A-0276 DC ground fault. Isolated to CB-B01-20, chafed home run against the rack. Repaired. Noted fw rev 4.3.0 in the service menu.

KVP24-2342D-0252 hard fault and would not restart. Went ahead and had a look at it and the DC contactor had failed, replaced it and the unit came back online. No recurrence through the end of the shift. There was a roadrunner sat on the skid steps when I pulled up which was a first for me.
B03 walkdown / 2 cracked glass
Fence and gate check done. The lens on camera 3 was fogged up so I wiped it down. Rest of the perimeter is sound.
tr-z08 annual, slew greased, backlash ok
kvp36-2423b-0262 dc gf, pinched connector cb-b02-24, rplcd
MGX33-1744D-0100 tripped on DC GF. Traced it to a pinched connector in CB-B09-14. Replaced the connector and the unit came back online. It has held since per SCADA. Nothing else showing in the log.

Soiling assessment carried out on B04. Soiling ratio reading around 5 percent against the reference cells, which is up from about 2 percent at the last assessment six weeks ago. Walked the block and the accumulation is fairly even, heavier on the lower third of each module as usual. Recommending this block goes in the next wash cycle rather than waiting for the scheduled one.

TR-B06-R096 was rotating rough through the morning sweep. Pulled the drive cover and the grease was dried out and gritty with it. Repacked it properly and it moves smooth now. Verified through a full sweep before leaving.
XFMR-B04 annual complete. LTC counter checked and recorded, gas relay clear, bushings cleaned down. No weeping or tracking anywhere on them per inspection.

Went ahead and reworked the sagging home runs over in B08 before the mow crew gets there, there were a fair few spans hanging low enough to get caught up, all clipped back out of the way now, the drive out was slow with the ice on the road
TR-Z07 annual; slew greased; backlash in spec
TR-B01-R027 damper bolt loose. Retorqued to spec and verified the row through a full sweep.
CB-B05-03 annual. Lugs torqued, IR clean, no hot spots.
TR-B05-R017 out of alignment, limits recalibrated

Called out after the storm came through overnight. Found water in two of the combiner skids over in B03. Isolated both and pumped them out. Both enclosures dried and the gland seals inspected: on one the lower gland had clearly failed, on the other the ingress was through the door seal which has perished along the bottom edge. Resealed the gland and ordered a replacement door seal. Both skids back in service. This row has now had four water ingress events and I would recommend the seals are replaced as a campaign.
gf continuity b01, all in range

Went ahead and did the PM on CES40-1828C-0361, cleaned the heat sinks off and checked the contactors over for pitting which there was none of on any of them. Got it logged and closed out and the unit was reporting normally when I left.
CB-B07-05 annual. Lugs torqued, IR scan clean, no hot spots.

Went out and did the snow clearing on the access roads and the skid pads over at B08, and it was a long job of it, the drift past the second gate was up over the hood on the truck and I had to sit and wait on the plow to get anywhere at all. The array was left to shed on its own per the procedure and it had mostly done that by the time I got out there anyway. Nothing damaged as far as I could see.
Cable management repair in B01. Wire runs had dropped into the mow path, resecured about six spans and clipped them clear of it. Most of the failures were at the clip fixing.

Quarterly site walk on B10. Cable sag noted on the north rows, roughly eight spans hanging lower than they should be. Will schedule the rework before the mow crew comes through. Rest of the block fine.

Got called out to an outage on B01 in the early hours and went ahead and drove out. Found a snake had got itself across the bus in the skid and that was the end of both of them. Cleaned all that up, which was not the nicest job I have had this year, and replaced what was damaged in there. Got it back in service before it got light. Somebody wants to look at how it got in there in the first place, the door seal at the bottom has a gap you could get a hand through.
Scheduled wash on B01 completed. Crew finished ahead of the wind advisory. Walked two rows behind them afterward, coverage good with no streaking on the lower edges.
Feeder relay tripped on B04. Found a failed termination in the switchgear, replaced it and back in service.

Post event walkdown on B04 following last night's weather. Walked all rows in the block. No structural damage found: no bent purlins, no displaced clamps, no glass breakage anywhere. Spot checked clamp torque on six positions in the outer rows, all within spec.

Went ahead and did the torque audit on B07, sampled thirteen rack bolts across the block and every one of them came back within tolerance, no retorquing needed. There was a rattlesnake under the second row that took a while to persuade to move on, other than that a quiet morning out there.
Finished the mowing on B06 and two rows on the south end had to be skipped because the ground is still too soft to take the machine down there safely
XFMR-B01 annual. LTC counter checked and recorded, gas relay clear, bushings cleaned down. No weeping or tracking anywhere on them.
TR-B01-R003 out of alignment, limits recalibrated
B05 clamp check / 6 below spec / retorqued
drone over B03, 2 open strings ticketed
RTU locked up overnight. Rebooted, points came back.
MET-01 irradiance reading flatlined so I went out and had a look at it, the sensor had failed outright so I swapped it for a new one and the readings came straight back where they should be
wash crew done b05, ag dust heavy on the lower rows
KVP24-1619B-0208 down on AC undervoltage. POI looked normal on the meters. Reset the unit and monitored it for two hours before leaving, no further trips.

Post event walkdown on B01 after last night's weather. Walked the whole block and there was no structural damage anywhere that I could find, nothing displaced and no glass broken. Nothing to report from this one.

KVP36-2342D-0300 threw a DC ground fault alarm. Isolated the fault down to CB-B06-02. Found a home run that had chafed through against the rack upright, the insulation was worn right down to the conductor. Repaired the run and resecured it clear of the steel with a proper standoff rather than just a tie. Unit returned to service and the fault has not recurred.
Scheduled wash on B08 completed, and the crew got finished ahead of the wind advisory that came in later that afternoon. Coverage looked alright on the rows I walked behind them.

Went ahead and did the tracker PM on TR-Z09, greased all the bearings down the zone and checked the damper bolts as part of it, two were loose so they got retorqued. There was a family of quail living under one of the rows which took some working around but no harm done to them or me.
CB-B10-22 string 5 reading zero. Blown fuse, replaced it and the current came back. Nothing else in the can.

Went out and did the annual inspection on CB-B04-08, and got the lugs torqued while I had it open. The IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere in the can. There is nothing much else to report on this one, it all looked as it should and I got it closed up and back in service without any trouble at all.
warranty case opened on kvp36-2422b-0175, oem want the fault logs first
slt25-1736c-0728 iso fault, damp am, cleared when dry

Went out and did the storm walkdown on B04 after the weather came through last night, the road down that side was still under water at the low crossing so I had to come round the top way to get there. kvp24-2347d-0323 dc gf, cb-b04-19, chafed home run, repaired
Ten broken modules in B04, replaced from spares. Rock strike from the mower.
comms alarm, everything online when i got there, historian gap only, no production impact

Went out to TR-Z07 where the controller had shown offline and I went ahead and power cycled the TCU at the zone cabinet. It came back up straight away and tracked normally through the rest of the afternoon after that. There was nothing obvious to say why it had dropped out in the first place.
Walked B06 for soiling. Dust accumulation moderate, not washing yet. Will look again next cycle.

Went up for the walkdown on B01 and had a good look round the block, and there was nothing significant to report from it at all, it all looked to be in reasonable order. Two modules with cracked glass which have gone on the punch list for the next round.
Burned connector on a home run in B05. Cut it back past the damage and reterminated. String current came back. That is the second one on this row.
Drone IR flight over B07. Two open strings found and ticketed separately. Rest of the block looked normal.
Annual inspection on CB-B03-16. Lugs torqued, IR scan clean with no hot spots in the can.
Quarterly site walk B03. Cable sag on the north rows, will schedule the rework. idk when.
TR-B03-R074 limit switch replaced. Row recalibrated and verified through a sweep.
PM on MGX33-2141D-0266. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors checked for pitting, none found. Logged and closed out.

Went out and did the PM on KVP24-1618B-0361 and got everything on the sheet done for it. The heat sinks were cleaned off and the contactors were checked over for pitting and there was none on any of them at all. Nothing else came up on it that would need following. Got it logged and closed out and the unit was reporting normally when I left.

Got called out to an outage on B01 and went out there. There was a snake got itself across the bus in the skid which was the end of it and the outage both. Cleaned all that up and replaced what was damaged in there. The door seal at the bottom of that skid has a gap in it which is presumably how it got in and somebody wants to deal with that.

RTU locked up overnight, the historian gap runs from roughly 0130 to 0715. Rebooted it just after eight and all the points came back. Second trip out here this week for the same box. No production impact, data only.
Oil sample pulled from XFMR-B09 and shipped for the DGA. Bushings look alright from the ground, no weeping on any of them.

Pulled the permit and did the LOTO before opening it up. CB-B02-09 low current alarm, there was water sat in the bottom of the enclosure which I drained out and the gland has been resealed. One fuse replaced. Permit closed at the end.

Pulled the permit before going into B02 to look at the units that keep dropping out. Same ones as last time and the time before. KVP36-2423B-0265 flagged a fan fault. Bird nest in the intake plenum, cleared it out.
TR-B07-R052 controller reset, back online. Verified through a sweep.
cb-b08-02 pm, ir clean, currents balanced
cb-b01-14 pm, dust in the gland, cleaned and resealed
KVP36-1631C-0342 failed to start when I got out to it. The IGBT module had failed which I replaced from the site spares, and it fired up fine after that and has held through the rest of the shift.
storm walk b03, few cracked glass tagged
b05 soiling ratio abt 6%, recommending wash next cycle

Went out to a string that was out in B03 and had a look at it. There was one module in it with the cells shattered up in one corner, glass still in one piece but the cells are gone. Swapped it out from the spares we have in the shop and the string came back up to where it should be. Nothing else in that row that I could see was any trouble.
KVP36-2410A-0190 is still under parts warranty. Opened a case with the OEM, waiting on the RMA.

KVP24-1932C-0327 threw a DC ground fault alarm, so I went out and isolated it down to CB-B07-20 where there was a home run chafed through against the rack, repaired it and got it resecured properly clear of the steel

MET-02 pyranometers and rain gauge cleaned. RSR releveled while I was up the mast.

Aerial IR survey flown over B06. Six hot cells flagged in the report, scattered across the block, nothing clustered on any string or row and none above the reporting threshold individually. gf up again in b04, second time, reseated connections, cleared
PM on KVP36-1701A-0226. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors checked, no pitting.

Vandalism along the road side again, several modules shot out. Documented each one with photographs and replaced fourteen from spares. Recommend the screening along that boundary is looked at, replacing modules three times a year is not sustainable.

Went out and did the perimeter inspection, and the fence is intact the whole way round except for a washout by the south gate where the drainage cuts under it, filled that in and packed it down same as last time, that culvert is undersized for what it takes and it will do it again

Went out and did the PM on KVP36-2415B-0291 this morning and got everything done that was on the sheet for it. The filters were pretty well loaded so I went ahead and swapped them out for a fresh set. Tested the fan bank while I was in there and all six of them are running as they should be, no noise off any of them. Unit was reporting normally when I closed it up and left.
Feeder relay tripped B01. Failed termination in the switchgear. Replaced.

Went ahead and reworked the sagging home runs over in B06 before the mow crew gets down there, there were a fair few spans hanging low enough to get caught up and they have all been clipped back out of the way now
Went out and dealt with a burned connector on one of the home runs in B04, cut it back and reterminated it, string came straight back. Cold out there but a clear morning for once.
Called out after the storm. Water in two of the combiner skids in B08, isolated both and pumped them out. Roads were bad getting down there.

Tracker fault came up on TR-Z11 so I went out to it, and there was no fault showing at all by the time I got there, the whole zone was tracking along with everything else and the controller was clear. Reset the flag and watched it through a move. Nothing else to report on it.
B06 walkdown. 2 cracked glass for punch list.

kvp36-1802a-0377 semiannual; filters; vacuum; torque; no issues
Post event walkdown B08 after last night's weather. No structural damage found anywhere in the block.

CB-B06-04 + adjacent; megger normal
MGX33-1724B-0257 HARD FAULT. Replaced the AC contacter and the invertor came back online, no recurrence through to the end of the shift. Nothing else showing in the fault log for it.
B06 walkdown. Nothing significant. Two cracked modules for the punch list.
MET-03 pyranometers and rain gauge cleaned. Releveled the RSR while I was up there, the bubble was well off. tbd on the logger battery.
TR-Z02 comm fault / reseated daisy chain / cleared

Washing crew completed B04 today. Ag dust was heavy on the lower rows before they started, heavier than we usually see this time of year. I walked a couple of rows behind them to check the coverage and it looked good. Crew signed out mid afternoon.
B03 site walk. Cable sag north rows. Will schedule.

MGX33-2408A-0213 DC ground fault alarm. Isolated the fault to CB-B10-03. Found a home run chafed through against the rack upright. Repaired the conductor and resecured it clear of the steel. Unit returned to service.
Copper theft attempt at B04. Fence cut and some grounding conductor taken. Report filed with the sheriff, fence patched and the conductor replaced the same day.

Went ahead and did the PM on MGX33-2436C-0117, the filters were loaded so they were swapped out for a fresh set, and the fan bank was tested with all six of them running as they should be. Nothing else came up on it.
Pulled nine modules from B06 for the warranty claim. Boxed and staged for pickup, photos and serials in the file.
kvp24-2116b-0107 pm complete. filters were loaded so swapped them out. fan bank tested, all six running as they should

Combiner PM on CB-B04-14. IR scan showed nothing anywhere in the can. String currents balanced per SCADA across all twenty four. Lugs torqued as part of the routine and none had moved since the last visit. Nothing to report.
8 modules pulled B04 for warranty / boxed + staged / photos filed
aerial ir survey b03, 7 hot cells flagged, scattered, nothing clustered. report going to the asset manager
tr-z02 drive regreased, third in this block this quarter, normal wear

kvp36-1911a-0305 pm, sinks, ok

string out b06; shattered cells; swapped

MGX33-2018B-0228 down on AC undervoltage. POI looked normal. Reset and monitored two hours.
xfmr-b08 annual done, ltc counter chkd, gas relay clear, bushings cleaned

Pre emergent application on B09. Started at the north end with the wind at around 6 mph which is inside the label limit. Buffer maintained at the drainage throughout. The remaining strip is scheduled for the next suitable morning.
CB-B04-17 PM; IR scan clean; currents balanced per scada

Mowing on B03. Growth was well ahead of schedule after the rain and the crew needed an extra day to get through the block properly. Walked behind them afterward on the two rows nearest the home run trench and there is no damage to any of the cabling. Two rows on the south end were left, ground too soft. Crew signed out at the end of the second day.
PM on KVP36-1630C-0101. Heat sinks cleaned, contactors checked for pitting, none found. Logged and closed out.
TR-Z05 lube chk ok

Did the PM on CES40-2220B-0216 today, cleaned the heat sinks down which were pretty dusty, checked the contactors over for any pitting and there was none that I could see on any of them, and got it logged and closed out, the wind was up all afternoon which made the cabinet doors a nuisance
Duplicate, see the other ticket.

Pulled the permit before going near it. CES40-1527C-0305 had tripped on AC overcurrent per the HMI. Reset the unit and it ran fine for the rest of the day with no further trips. Went back through the fault log and there is no pattern to it that I could see. Permit closed at the end of the shift.
Near miss reported. Contractor entered B05 without checking in for the LOTO. Stood the crew down and rebriefed.
kvp36-2419b-0371 hard fault; igbt rplcd; back online

MV cable fault between B04 and the collector, and the locator put it at about 300 ft in from the block end. Got both ends isolated and grounded and tagged out for now. Torque audit on B06. Sampled four rack bolts, all within tolerance. No retorquing required.

TR-Z03 was stuck out at -30 degrees when I got to it, the motor was pulling high current on the meter so I replaced it and the row is tracking again with the rest of the block now, that is the third motor off that zone in about eighteen months which somebody ought to have a look at
TR-B04-R023 drive motor replaced. Row tracking normally, verified through a full sweep before leaving.

Did the quarterly torque check on the module clamps over in B06 and ten of them came back below spec which is about average for that block, retorqued all of them to 18 Nm, the rest of what I sampled was within tolerance, and there was a fair bit of wind up which made the wrench readings a nuisance to hold steady on the outer rows
Vandalism, several modules shot out along the road side. Documented the lot with photos and replaced twelve of them from spares. Same stretch as last time. Report filed.
Module clamp torque sweep on B01. Found a run of loose clamps concentrated on the east rows, retorqued all of them to spec per the HMI record.
PM on MGX33-1936C-0254. Heat sinks cleaned down, contactors checked for pitting, none found. Nothing else noted on the unit. Logged and closed out per procedure.
CB-B04-16 str 9 zero / fuse / rplcd

drone over b09, 2 open strings ticketed

GF continuity B04 / all in range

reworked sagging home runs b07 ahead of the mow crew

TR-B04-R083 damper bolt loose. Retorqued to spec and verified the row through a sweep.
wash b01 done, ahead of the wind advisory

Did the PM on KVP36-1922B-0140 and got everything on the sheet done, the filters were loaded so they were swapped for a fresh set and the fan bank was tested with all six running as they should be. Firmware on this one is 5.2.1 which matches the rest of the block.
CB-B05-03 PM. Found dust ingress on the lower gland, cleaned it out and resealed. Fuses all good and currents balanced.
SLT25-2550D-0914 not reporting / reseated comms module + RS485 / ok
Cleared the volunteer growth along the fence at B02. Several had grown into the fabric and had to be cut out rather than just trimmed back.

Went out and did the PM on CES40-2147D-0188 and got everything on the sheet done for it. The heat sinks were cleaned off and the contactors were checked over for pitting, and there was none on any of them at all. Got it logged and closed out.
MGX33-2439C-0115 flagged a fan fault. Bird nest in the intake plenum, cleared it out. Fans fine after.
Fourteen broken modules in B01, replaced from spares. Damage consistent with rock strike from mowing.
TR-Z03 annual service. Greased the slew drive and checked the backlash, within spec throughout.
Drone IR flight over B07. Two open strings found, ticketed separately. Rest looked normal.

GF continuity B08. All in range.
Storm walkdown on B03 after the weather. A few modules with cracked glass which I have tagged for replacement. Everything else in the block looked fine. idk when the punch list gets worked.

GF testing on CB-B04-19 and the adjacent cans. Megger readings all normal. Nothing to report on any of them.

Semiannual PM on KVP36-2445D-0121. Filters replaced, cabinet vacuumed out, and the torque check on the DC bus completed with everything within spec. Nothing came up needing following on it.
