They authorised the swap and the part has shipped from the depot. There was a coyote hanging about by the skid the whole time I was out there. Unit is isolated and tagged until the part turns up.
Second overtemp on KVP36-2422B-0175 this season. Reset it again. Checked the intake and the heat sinks, both clear per inspection.

Went up and did the walkdown on B09 and there was nothing significant to report from the block itself, it all looked reasonable enough. Two modules with cracked glass which have gone on the punch list for the next round.

Row TR-Z05 was out of alignment with the rest of the block, noticed it on the morning sweep. Came back after lunch with the laptop and recalibrated the limits. Tracking normal now, watched it through two moves before I left.
Went out and did the pre emergent on B04, the wind was borderline all morning so I held off on the west edge and did the rest of it, will pick up that strip another day when it drops
kvp24-2136c-0086 dc gf, cb-b07-07, chafed home run, repaired
Torque audit B08. Sampled twelve rack bolts, all within tolerance. No retorquing required.
TR-B03-R021 was stuck out at 52 degrees. Motor drawing high current on the meter so it was replaced and the row is tracking again with the rest of the block.
Comms alarm came in overnight, everything was online again by the time I got out there. Historian gap only, no production impact at all.
grid fault ride through took ces40-2417b-0242 offline. it had cleared on its own before i got out there. verified output normal against the neighbours, nothing to do on it
Comms alarm came in overnight, everything was already back online by the time I got out there. Historian gap only, no production impact from any of it.
Lightning took out the comms and a surge card overnight. Partial monitoring restored by mid afternoon, the rest tomorrow when the card comes in.

Torque audit on B04. Sampled ten rack bolts spread across the rows, all came back within tolerance so there was no retorquing needed on it. The LOTO was not required for this one and the permit was closed at the end.
Post emergent on B07, spot treated along the fence line same as last time, records are in the binder and the containers were rinsed and disposed of properly

Two fuses out in CB-B01-11, replaced both from the truck. Checked the strings and the terminations either side for a cause and found nothing at all: no water, no chafing, connectors all sound. Currents verified balanced on restoration. No explanation for it.
TR-B03-R032 stuck out at 60 degrees. Motor drawing high current, replaced it. Row tracking again.
TR-Z01 lube + fastener chk, ok
Vandalism. Several modules shot out along the road side. Documented and replaced six.
mgx33-1714b-0183 gf, walked strings, nothing, meggered ok, reset held, rev 6.0.0
Annual inspection on CB-B09-14. Lugs torqued, IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere in the can. String currents balanced.

Site tripped overnight. Relay targets pointed at the main feeder. Walked the whole collector run and the switchgear and there was nothing visible anywhere, no damage, no tracking, nothing burned. Restored under supervision mid morning and it has held since. No root cause established.
TR-B06-R033 PM; bearings greased; 2 damper bolts loose
TR-Z08 tracker PM. Bearings greased, damper bolts checked, two were loose and retorqued.

Went out to CB-B02-01 where string 6 was reading zero, and it was just a blown fuse which I replaced and the current came straight back up. Nothing else wrong in the can that I could see. Quiet morning out there for once.

Finished the mowing on B01 today, two rows down on the south end got skipped because the ground is still too soft to take the machine, there is a seep down there that never seems to dry out properly, will pick those up on the next pass when it firms up a bit
tr-z05 tcu offline, power cycled, back tracking

Row TR-Z05 had come out of alignment with the rest of the block again, and I went ahead and recalibrated the limits on it and it is tracking normal now. That zone is on the exposed side of the site and I suspect the wind is walking it out of position over time. There was a bobcat sat up on the end of the row watching me do the whole thing.
CES40-2211A-0237 failed to start when I got out to it. The DC contactor had failed which I replaced from the site spares, and it fired up fine after that and has held since. tbd on the old one.
TR-B08-R003 annual service. Greased the slew drive, checked backlash, within spec.

Went out to CB-B01-06 where string 6 was reading zero on the portal and it was just a blown fuse which I replaced and the current came straight back up, had a look for a cause while I was in there and there was nothing obvious anywhere at all
ces40-2040d-0406 dc gf, cb-b04-06, chafed home run, repaired

KVP24-1912A-0220 tripped on AC overcurrent per the HMI at 1508. Reset the unit and it ran fine for the remainder of the day with no further trips. Went back through the fault log and there is no pattern to it that I can see. Temperture in the skid was up but not unusual for the time of year.
washed b04, up abt 4% next clear day
SLT25-1916B-0583 off network again. Cycled at the disconnect.
lost scada b02, fiber run tested bad, patched around it on the spare pair

Half the string inverters in B04 showed offline overnight and every one of them was back up and reporting by the time I got out there. Humidity was high overnight which these seem to do it in. No production loss at all as far as the meter goes.
Trimmed back the treeline south of B02. Contractor has left the brush again where it fell, chasing them on it. Second trip out here this week.
B08 clamp check, 12 below spec, retorqued to 18 Nm

TR-Z10 was squealing on the east sweep, same as the others on that block have been doing, the old grease had separated out and gone hard so I cleaned it all out and repacked it properly. These older rows are all about due for it and I would say the rest of the zone wants doing before they start making the same noise rather than us going out one at a time.
CB-B09-21 PM. Dust ingress on the lower gland, cleaned it out and resealed. Fuses all good, currents balanced.
CES40-1836C-0238 AC overcurrent / reset / fine after
CES40-1839C-0345 semiannual / filters / vacuum / torque / ok
Reworked the sagging home runs over in B09 before the mow crew gets down there, they had dropped low enough in a good few places to be a problem, all clipped back up now
High cabinet temp on CES40-2440D-0283. Filters were completely blocked, no airflow through them at all. Cleaned them out and the temp came back down within the half hour.

Ground fault came up on CES40-2413A-0175 so I went out and walked all the strings on it looking for a cause, there was nothing obvious anywhere at all, no chafing and no pinched connectors that I could find, meggered the lot and the readings came back fine so I reset it and it has held since
Nine broken modules in B09, replaced from spares. Rock strike off the mower by the look of it.
B03 site walk. Cable sag on the north rows. Will schedule.
Ground fault on KVP24-1906A-0149. Walked the strings, nothing obvious anywhere. Meggered ok, reset and it held.
tracker fault on TR-B06-R078, nothing wrong when i got there, row was tracking with the rest of the block. reset the flag and watched it through a couple of moves. fine
rtu locked, rebooted, points back
Went ahead and cleaned the soiling station on MET-02 and wiped down the reference cell, and the data had looked stuck so I power cycled the logger and it came back moving.
kvp36-2432c-0354 igbt failed, in warranty so opened a case with kelvara first, they authorised the swap, part coming from depot
TR-B04-R027 greased and fasteners checked. Nothing found out of order on the row.
Outage on B06. Snake across the bus in the skid. Cleaned up and replaced what was damaged.
KVP36-2432C-0356 IGBT failure, unit is inside the parts warranty so opened a case with Kelvara before touching it. They authorised the swap, part shipped from the depot.
lost scada b05, fiber bad, patched around it
CX-R06 chkd. Coolant loop and door seals fine.
TR-Z07 stuck at 25 degrees. Motor drawing high current, replaced it. Row tracking again.
Quarterly site walk on B03. Cable sag noted on the north rows which will want scheduling. Came back after lunch to finish the far end.
TR-Z03 lubrication and fastener check done. Nothing unusual anywhere on the zone.
Annual inspection on CB-B01-21. Lugs torqued, IR scan came back clean with no hot spots anywhere in the can.
Oil sample pulled from XFMR-B01 and shipped off for the DGA. Bushings look fine visually, no weeping or tracking on any of them. Results back in about two weeks.

TR-B05-R084 was squealing on the east sweep, same as the others on that block have been doing, the old grease had separated out and gone hard so I cleaned it all out and repacked it properly. These older rows are all about due for it, that is four now off this block this quarter, and I would say the rest of them want doing before they start making the same noise rather than us going out one at a time as they do.
kvp36-2025b-0337 fan fault, bird nest in the intake plenum, cleared it out
kvp36-2435c-0234 wouldnt open the dc side. dc contactor welded shut. rplcd it. contacts badly pitted, looked like its been running hot a while

Did the torque audit on B05 and sampled four rack bolts across the block, and every one of them came back within tolerance so there was no retorquing needed. Quiet morning out there, the snow had mostly gone off the access road.
Module wash on B05 with the two truck crew and the DI water. Output up about 5 percent on the next clear day per SCADA. Coverage looked good on the rows I walked afterward.
KVP36-2421B-0197 fan bank all running but airflow across the stack felt low. Pulled and cleaned the filters, they were not that dirty. Temps came down some. 103 out there.

Drone IR flight over B04 completed this morning. Two open strings were found in the imagery and both have been ticketed separately for somebody to go and look at. Rest of the block came back looking normal enough. Good conditions for flying.
cb-b03-19 string 6 zero, blown fuse, rplcd
KVP36-2428C-0165 hard faulted. IGBT module 2 had clear thermal damage, discoloured and the busbar heat marked. Replaced the module and the gate driver.

Went ahead and had a look at CB-B03-16 where string 2 was reading zero, and it was just a blown fuse which I replaced and the current came straight back up. There was a roadrunner sat on top of the combiner when I pulled up which was a first. Nothing else wrong in the can.

Storm walkdown on B01 following the weather Tuesday night. Walked all rows in the block. Found four modules with cracked glass, all on the outer two rows facing the prevailing direction, tagged them for replacement and photographed each one. No racking damage, no displaced clamps, no wiring pulled down. Torque spot checked on six clamps in the affected rows, all still within spec. Nothing else to report from this block.
KVP36-1922B-0138 tripped DC GF. Traced to a pinched connector in CB-B06-09. Replaced, back online.

Went ahead and did the post event walkdown on B03 after the weather last night and there was no structural damage anywhere in the block that I could see. The road in was still under water at the low crossing so I came round the top way. Nothing to report on this one.

Had a near miss reported to me this morning. A contractor had gone into B08 without checking in and without the LOTO on the skid being verified, which is not the first time we have had this with that crew. Went ahead and stood the whole crew down for the rest of the morning and rebriefed everyone on the check in procedure before letting them back to work.
KVP36-2434C-0084 hard faulted. IGBT 1 cooked, busbar heat marked. Swapped module and gate driver.
